Fresh out of OTC, {name} walks into the compound. Nobody salutes, nobody says hi. A guy with a beard points at an empty locker. What will you do?
You kept your mouth shut. An old operator nodded at you. That is basically a hug here.
You won a few smiles. One guy even remembered your name.
They nicknamed you "Cruise Director." It will stick for years.
You wake at 0300 sweating, dreaming you are still on the Long Walk in West Virginia with a 45 lb ruck and no idea of the time limit. What will you do?
Go for a 5 a.m. ruck anyway
You walked it off. The Appalachians are still in your knees.
You remembered you passed. Nobody can take that away. You slept like a rock.
For the first time in your career, nobody cares about your hair. {buddy} bets you can't grow a beard by the next deployment. What will you do?
Your beard came in thick and terrifying. {buddy} paid up.
Your beard came in patchy. You look like a substitute teacher. {buddy} took your money.
You stayed clean-cut. In a foreign airport, you look exactly like a soldier. Not ideal.
Your mom calls and asks what your new job is. The answer is classified. She sounds hurt. What will you tell her?
You lied for her own good. She bought it. Mostly.
She got the hint and promised never to ask again.
She told her book club. The security office called you in for a chat.
In the shoot house you clear your corner but put two rounds into a "no-shoot" target holding a phone. The cadre is staring. What will you do?
You admitted the mistake. The cadre respected that more than the miss.
Nobody here accepts excuses. You ran the house twenty more times that night.
Ammo here seems unlimited. You could shoot until your hands bleed or go home early for once. What will you do?
Your split times dropped. Your thumbs are raw hamburger.
You had dinner with real humans. Novel experience.
You are told to blend in overseas. You own exactly one outfit: cargo shorts, Oakleys, and a tactical belt. What will you do?
{buddy} took you shopping. You now own jeans with no extra pockets.
A street kid yelled "AMERICAN SOLDIER!" before you even left the airport.
You are slotted for advanced breaching. The instructor wants someone to stand closer than feels reasonable to "feel the charge." What will you do?
The blast rattled your teeth but you learned exactly how much is too much.
Your ears rang for a week. Mild TBI flagged by medical.
You watched and learned. Smart, but quiet guys notice who hangs back.
Your special pay hits. You have never had this much money. A dealership has a lifted truck with your name on it. What will you do?
It is gorgeous. It also costs more than your car insurance and rent combined.
Future you will be grateful. Present you drives a 2009 Corolla.
On a freefall refresher, your altimeter reads wrong and you are not sure of your altitude. What will you do?
You opened early and drifted away from the group. Embarrassing but alive.
You read the ground perfectly and landed right on the X.
You pulled late, had a hard opening and broke your ankle on landing.
A grizzled operator corners you at the team room fridge and starts a story that begins in 1993. It is 1900 on Friday. What will you do?
Two hours later, you learned more than in all of OTC.
You escaped. He knows you faked it.
Your first raid on a high-value target in {country}. You are third man in the stack. The door is about to blow. What will you do?
Textbook. Target captured, zero shots fired. You barely remember any of it.
A guard fired through a wall. Shrapnel caught your thigh. Your first Purple Heart.
You moved fast and it worked. The team leader is annoyed but impressed.
You broke the flow. Nobody got hurt but the debrief was brutal.
Your cousin tags you in a photo from the gym with the caption "my brother the secret agent lol." What will you do?
It is gone. Your cousin thinks you are paranoid. You are paid to be.
Security found it. You spent a week scrubbing your digital life with a very unamused officer.
You are offered six months of language school before your next rotation. It means less trigger time. What will you do?
You can now order coffee and interrogate a suspect in a second language.
You kept shooting. Someone else got the slot.
{buddy} swaps your practice target for a cutout of your team sergeant. You hit it twice in the face. What will you do?
Everybody laughed, including the team sergeant. Eventually.
The glitter got in a sensitive item. The sergeant major was not amused.
Your partner asks why you vanished for three weeks with no phone. "Training" is wearing thin. What will you do?
She accepted it, but you can tell she is keeping score.
She ended it. "I can't date a ghost," she said.
Bring her to a family day
Meeting the other spouses helped. She gets it now, without knowing anything.
You are trying to keep up with a 42-year-old operator who deadlifts like a hydraulic press. Your back is already twitching. What will you do?
You pulled it. He grunted. That counts as approval.
Your lower back seized. Two weeks with a physical therapist named Brenda.
You stayed healthy. Ego bruised, spine intact.
You must follow a "target" across a city without being made. He just stopped and turned around. What will you do?
He scanned right past you. You also got a decent latte.
He walked in behind you and said "Hi." Fail.
Bold. He never suspected the guy who walked right past.
You made eye contact for too long. Burned.
The Unit lets you pick most of your own kit. A buddy recommends a brand-new optic nobody has tested in combat. What will you do?
Boring and reliable. Exactly what you want at 2 a.m. in a hallway.
It is incredible. Half the troop copies you.
It fogged up on the first cold night. You shot iron sights and swore a lot.
In a full-scale hostage rescue drill on a mock airliner, a role-player "hostage" bolts toward you. What will you do?
Correct. Everyone is a threat until proven otherwise.
He was the hijacker. Your team was "killed." Long debrief.
A "tactical influencer" offers you $2,000 to appear in a gun video, face blurred, no unit mentioned. What will you do?
You declined. Quiet professionals stay quiet.
Nobody figured it out. You feel a little dirty anyway.
Your distinctive tattoo gave you away. NJP and a lecture you will never forget.
Your convoy of unmarked vehicles in {country} gets hit by an IED and small arms. Your vehicle is on fire. What will you do?
You pulled him through flames under fire. Bronze Star with V.
You got him out but took burns on both arms.
You suppressed the ambush until the team broke contact.
You have had six energy drinks during a 30-hour mission planning cycle. Your heart is doing drum solos. What will you do?
The medic made you drink water and lie down. Embarrassing but fine.
You survived. You also saw sounds for a while.
Heart palpitations put you in the hospital for observation.
Evasive driving course: you must J-turn a sedan at speed. The instructor promises it is "basically safe." What will you do?
Perfect 180. You want to do this for a living now.
You rolled it. The roll cage worked. Your neck did not.
Go easy on the first try
Clean but slow. The instructor yawned.
On a training trip abroad, a drunk local shoves {buddy} at a bar. You are in civilian cover. What will you do?
You left before it escalated. Cover intact.
One punch, then you vanished. Nobody filed a report.
Police got involved. An embassy official had to bail you out. Huge mess.
A guy you went through Selection with, who quit on day 20, calls asking how to try again. What will you do?
You spent weekends with him in the woods. He feels ready.
Tell him you can't discuss it
Technically correct. He thinks you got arrogant.
The recce troop needs a new sniper. The pipeline is long and brutal, and you would leave your assault team. What will you do?
You made it. You can now hit a dinner plate at 1,000 yards.
You washed out on the stalk. Back to the assault team.
Under NODs on a rooftop in {country}, you lose depth perception near a ledge. What will you do?
You froze for a second and felt the edge with your boot. Smart.
You kept pace and the target was secured.
You stepped off a 12-foot roof. Broken wrist, cracked ribs.
A partner-force commander gifts you an ornate dagger after a joint op. Accepting gifts is a gray area. What will you do?
Report it to the legal team
Legal logged it. It hangs in the team room now.
Nobody asked. It looks great on your shelf.
An inventory audit found it. Paperwork, NJP and a lot of explaining.
HALO infiltration at 25,000 feet over {country}. Your oxygen mask starts leaking at exit. What will you do?
You tracked hard and stayed conscious. Landed on target.
Hypoxia made you loopy. You landed 3 km off and twisted a knee.
killed by hypoxia during a HALO jump
You blacked out. Your AAD fired your reserve. You woke in a field, alive by luck.
You are asked to be a role-player for current Selection candidates. You could make their lives miserable. What will you do?
You gave them a fair, hard test. The cadre appreciated it.
One candidate will remember your fake accent for the rest of his life.
Before a sensitive op, you realize your personal phone is still in your pocket. Location services are on. What will you do?
Embarrassing, but the comms guy caught it before step-off. Lesson learned.
Nothing happened. Your heart rate did, though.
It pinged a tower. The op was scrubbed. You were busted down a grade.
You are offered team leader of a four-man element. It means more planning and less time with your rifle. What will you do?
You are now responsible for three lives besides your own. Heavy.
You stayed in the stack. Simple life.
You are cadre for Assessment & Selection in West Virginia. A candidate is clearly hurt but refuses to quit. What will you do?
He hated you. The doctor found a stress fracture. You were right.
He finished. He will be a legend someday.
He collapsed on the trail with rhabdo. Investigation.
{buddy} is showing up smelling like whiskey after the last rotation. Nobody has said anything. What will you do?
He broke down and agreed to see the embedded psych. You may have saved his career.
He told you to mind your business. Things are tense now.
He got help, but he knows it was you.
It is not your business. Until it is.
Terrorists hold six aid workers in a compound in {country}. You lead the assault team. Intel is thin. What will you do?
All six hostages walked out. Every captor is down. Silver Star.
A sentry spotted you. Hostages saved, but you took a round through the shoulder.
Two days later, a drone confirmed positions and the rescue went clean. You barely slept.
A new operator on your team keeps hesitating in the shoot house. The troop sergeant major asks your opinion. What will you do?
Ask for time to mentor him
Two months of extra reps and he is now one of the fastest on the team.
He still froze on a real op. He was quietly sent back to the regular Army.
Brutal but honest. Standards are standards.
A New York publisher offers $400,000 for your memoir about the Unit. Security review would gut half of it. What will you do?
The team respects you for it. The money stings a little.
Write it and submit for review
Approved after redactions. You are rich and a little shunned.
Review dragged on for two years. Publisher walked.
Somehow nobody sued. Your former teammates do not return calls.
The government seized your profits and court-martialed you.
Your troop hits a bomb-maker's safe house in {country}. He is running out the back toward a car. What will you do?
You took him down in the dirt. Intelligence windfall. Bronze Star.
You got him but he had a knife. Twelve stitches in your forearm.
The car went nowhere. He surrendered.
At Thanksgiving, your uncle asks if you "killed anybody over there." Everyone goes quiet. What will you do?
You asked about his fantasy football team. Crisis averted.
You sat in the truck for 20 minutes. Your wife brought you pie.
He will never ask again. Your mom is mortified.
During a live-fire exercise, a ricochet hits {buddy} in the leg. Blood is pumping. What will you do?
Your tourniquet saved his life. ARCOM for quick action.
He lived but lost the leg. You replay it every night.
The medic got there in time, barely. You froze. You know it.
You come home from an 8-month rotation to find divorce papers on the counter. What will you do?
Counseling worked. You are both trying.
It did not work. She got the house.
You signed. The Unit is your family now. That is the problem.
A Navy SEAL team gets credit for a target your troop found and fixed. The press release names them. What will you do?
Quiet professionals. You know what you did.
JSOC quietly corrected the record internally.
You came off as petty. The general said "We are all on the same team."
Your team is pinned on a rooftop in {country} by an RPK on the next building. Two men are hit. What will you do?
You jumped the gap and silenced the gun. Silver Star.
killed by machine gun fire on a rooftop
Spooky erased the building. Your guys got medevaced.
The gunship was delayed. One of your wounded died.
Your team wants matching tattoos with a skull and the troop's call sign. It could identify you overseas. What will you do?
They grumbled. They also stay unidentifiable.
It looks fantastic. The intel guys sighed.
You see partner-force soldiers in {country} beating a detainee after a raid. They outnumber your team. What will you do?
You stopped it and filed the report. The partner commander is furious. You sleep fine.
You told yourself it was not your fight. It haunts you.
Fifteenth rotation. You cannot remember the last time you felt anything. The psych offers you a break. What will you do?
You fished, slept, and laughed. You feel human again.
You kept going. Your wife says you are a stranger.
A cadre member tells you Selection standards are being "adjusted" to pass more people. What will you do?
Your concerns were heard. Standards held.
You got the "stay in your lane" talk.
Not your call. You just hope the next guy is good.
The supply guy says your team's night vision upgrade is "backordered" while another troop got theirs. What will you do?
Bring him a case of beer
Someone saw. Gift to supply personnel = paperwork.
You got them in three weeks and lost a friend in supply.
A captured bomb-maker in {country} smirks and says there is another device ticking. Your team wants to "persuade" him. What will you do?
The professionals got the location by playing nice. The device was disarmed.
He talked. You feel sick about it.
He reported abuse. A JAG investigation ended your career.
Your spine is fused at two levels. The surgeon says one more hard jump could paralyze you. A big op is next week. What will you do?
You watched the op from the TOC. The team did fine without you.
You made it through. Your back screamed for a month.
You landed wrong. Months of rehab.
{buddy} was killed last year. His widow asks if you can teach his son to fish this summer. What will you do?
The kid laughs like his dad. It hurts and heals at the same time.
You could not face it. The check helped, but she noticed.
The range is behind schedule. Someone suggests skipping the final explosive safety check to make the window. What will you do?
Finished late. Nobody died. Good day.
It worked out. You got lucky.
A misfire cooked off near you. Wounded, and a safety investigation found your shortcut.
A poker game in the team room has gotten serious. One guy is down $8,000. What will you do?
The team grumbled but money problems kill clearances.
You cleaned house. Everybody hates you a little.
You lost your truck payment. And then some.
A real airliner is seized at a European airport. Your squadron spins up. You are on the first bird out. What will you do?
Lead the assault on the aircraft
You entered through the over-wing exits. 140 passengers lived. Bronze Star.
A hijacker fired once. You stopped him, but the round found you.
You held the perimeter while the assault went in clean.
A buddy from your Ranger days asks you to vouch for him at Selection. He is decent, not great. What will you do?
He did not get in. He is still your friend. Mostly.
He made it and proved you right.
He quit on day 3. Your judgment is now in question.
You keep dreaming about a doorway in {country} where things went wrong. You are snapping at your kids. What will you do?
It is slow, but you are sleeping again.
It works for an hour. Then it really does not.
A journalist publishes details of your last op. Investigators ask who on your team talks to reporters. You have a suspicion. What will you do?
You were right. The team is shaken but intact.
The leaker was never found. Trust is lower in the team room now.
A tunnel complex in {country} may hold an HVT. Nobody wants to go in first. What will you do?
You found him hiding at a dead end. Bronze Star.
killed by a booby trap in a tunnel
A tripwire went off in the dark.
The dog found him in 90 seconds. Good boy.
As cadre, you see a candidate cheat on a land nav leg by following a road. Nobody else saw. What will you do?
He was dropped. Integrity is the real test.
He made it through. You will wonder about him forever.
You are being considered for squadron sergeant major. It would mean leaving the assault line for good. What will you do?
You are now the most respected NCO in the squadron. You miss the breach.
You turned it down. The old guys get it.
You train a partner counterterror unit in {country}. Their commander wants you to join a raid "just to watch." What will you do?
They did fine. Your training showed.
You helped them clear a building. A legend was born.
Your presence was unauthorized. Huge headache for the ambassador.
You arrive as a new troop commander. Your senior NCO has been in the Unit longer than you have been in the Army. What will you do?
Your NCOs decided you are "one of the good ones."
They let you fail on a training op. Message received.
You have six hours to plan a raid on a compound in {country}. The intel package conflicts on the number of guards. What will you do?
You brought extra shooters. Turned out you needed them.
Intel was right. Fast and clean.
Twice as many guards. Two of your men were wounded.
You brief the JSOC commander on a plan. He asks a question you cannot answer. The room is silent. What will you do?
He respected the honesty. You had the answer in an hour.
He knew you were bluffing. Career ice is thin now.
The HVT is in a building with women and children. A strike is available now; a raid risks your men. What will you do?
The raid got hot. You and two operators were hit.
He moved a day later. Strike on an empty road. Patience paid.
Target killed. You will see the BDA photos forever.
A congressman visits the compound and wants a photo with "real Delta guys." Your men refuse. What will you do?
He got a photo with a mannequin wearing kit. Close enough.
Face blurred. Still, your men think less of you.
Evaluation season. You must rank three outstanding officers and only one can get the top block. What will you do?
Fair and painful. One of them stopped saying hi to you.
Favor the one up for promotion
Strategic. He got promoted. The others noticed.
Your team grabbed a laptop on a raid. Analysts want it now; your men want to hit the next target tonight using its files. What will you do?
Three raids in one night. The network collapsed.
The second target was a dry hole. The enemy is spooked now.
Slower, but they found a goldmine.
Customs officials in {country} question your team's documents. One operator is visibly sweating. What will you do?
You chatted about football. Waved through.
Detained for six hours until the embassy made calls. The trip was blown.
It got sorted, but the cover is now thinner.
Your Black Hawk takes fire on approach in {country}. The pilot asks: abort or insert? What will you do?
You fought onto the objective and captured the target. Bronze Star.
killed when his helicopter was shot down
The aircraft was hit on landing.
Everyone lived. The target lived too.
You sit on the commander's board for a candidate who passed everything but seems arrogant. What will you do?
Ego kills teams. You trust your gut.
He grew up fast. Good operator.
He got a teammate hurt within a year. You think about it.
You need new breaching equipment. The paperwork requires a 40-page justification. What will you do?
Have a staff NCO write it
Done in two days. He did a better job than you would have.
Lawyers rewrote the ROE. Your men think it will get someone killed. What will you do?
The ROE was clarified. The team trusts you more.
You were told to "comply and execute."
Rules are rules. The team grumbles.
A sandstorm rolls in during a mission window in {country}. Aviation says it is your call. What will you do?
The storm covered your approach. Total surprise.
A hard landing in brownout. Injuries across the chalk.
Two operators' wives are feuding. It is spilling into the team room. What will you do?
The chaplain earned his paycheck that week.
It got worse before it got better.
An American family is held on a yacht off the coast of {country}. The SEALs are busy. Your troop gets the call. What will you do?
Plan a joint op with the Navy
Boats and snipers worked together. Everyone rescued. Bronze Star.
Negotiations collapsed before you could move. A tragic outcome.
They handled it. You tracked from the TOC.
The US ambassador in {country} wants your operators to stay inside the embassy compound. Your mission requires movement. What will you do?
You won her over with a detailed risk brief.
The mission slowed down. Diplomacy wins today.
Your helo lands at the wrong compound. Residents are panicking. What will you do?
You got out. The real target was alerted.
Move on foot to the real target
You ran 800 meters and caught him leaving.
His guards were ready for you.
One of your best operators was caught stealing cash from a raid site. He swears it was for a dead buddy's family. What will you do?
He was released from the Unit. You did the right thing. It hurt.
He returned the money. Nobody found out.
Investigators found it anyway. You were charged too.
A huge multinational counterterror exercise. Your foreign counterparts keep showing off. What will you do?
Your team quietly won every scenario.
You crushed them. Beers were bought.
They won. Their sniper was ridiculous.
The CIA says the HVT is in town A. Your own sources say town B. You only get one shot. What will you do?
Town A was right. He is gone.
The flight doc spots a heart irregularity on your EKG. A full workup could ground you. What will you do?
It was benign. You are cleared.
You had an episode on a ruck march. Months of recovery.
You are offered a second tour as squadron operations officer. Your family wants you home more. What will you do?
Great for your career. Your kids barely recognize you.
You go to every soccer game. You miss the Unit daily.
Insurgents in {country} claim to hold one of your men. Proof of life is uncertain. What will you do?
You brought him home alive. Silver Star.
killed during a personnel recovery mission
It was a hoax. Your guy was safe all along.
Your interpreter mistranslates a key phrase during a tense standoff with local militia. What will you do?
You defused it with a smile and a cigarette.
Shots were fired. A quick firefight.
Nobody died. You need a better interpreter.
A news site reports your troop's location. Higher suspects someone in your chain. What will you do?
It was a staffer in DC. You were cleared.
Investigators took a closer look at you because of it.
A helicopter goes down near your position. You are the closest unit. What will you do?
You fought through a city to reach them. Every crewman lived. DSC.
The city came alive around you.
The QRF took 40 minutes. Not everyone made it.
You take command of the Unit. Your first decision: approve a risky high-value raid tonight or wait for better intel. What will you do?
It went bad. You have letters to write.
Prudent. The target will turn up again.
You testify in a closed Senate session about a failed op. A senator asks if you would do it again. What will you do?
You sounded like a politician. They noticed.
The Pentagon wants to cut your aviation support by 20%. What will you do?
You brief the President in the Situation Room. He asks for your honest odds of success. What will you do?
He appreciated it. The op was approved.
It failed. Your optimism is now in the press.
A major newspaper wants a profile on the Unit's commander. The Army says it is up to you. What will you do?
They quoted you out of context.
You are on the shortlist for brigadier general, but it means leaving special operations. What will you do?
An inspector general report criticizes your command climate. What will you do?
A British SAS commander proposes a joint op in {country}. Political risks are high. What will you do?
You add a name to the memorial wall. His family asks you to speak at the service. What will you do?
You barely got through it. They thanked you.
Ask his team leader to speak
He knew him best. It was right.
A defense contractor offers you a $600K/year job after retirement, wink wink, if you favor their bid now. What will you do?
The IG thanked you. Integrity intact.
Nothing traced back. You feel dirty.
A hurricane hits North Carolina. The compound is damaged and your neighbors need help. What will you do?
Your old troop holds a reunion. Stories get exaggerated. Someone tells your story wrong. What will you do?
You are now a legend. Factually incorrect, but a legend.
A Gold Star family asks you to speak at their son's high school about service. What will you do?
The kids were spellbound. Three asked about enlisting.
You could not do it. They understood.
Surprise urinalysis. You took a friend's "sleep gummy" last weekend. What will you do?
It was melatonin. Awkward but fine.
It had THC in it. NJP.
A charity ruck for fallen operators. 40 miles. Your knees are 40 years old. What will you do?
Your knee gave out at mile 28.
You handed out water. Still meaningful.
Your personal email was hacked. The attacker may have photos of you in uniform. What will you do?
Your photos showed up on a foreign forum.
Your father had a stroke. You are on alert for a short-notice deployment. What will you do?
You were at his bedside. He recovered partially.
You deployed. He passed while you were gone.
A training exercise requires a disguise. The only thing in the prop room is a mullet wig and a fanny pack. What will you do?
Nobody looked twice at the guy in the mullet.
You were spotted in eight seconds.
You've been assigned to the dining facility. A mountain of greasy trays awaits and the cook is already yelling. How do you handle it?
You finished early. The cook grunted, which counts as praise.
You napped behind the flour sacks. Nobody noticed.
The cook found you. You now own the grease trap for a week.
Best sheet cake of your life. Worth it.
Caught with frosting on your face. Extra hours added.
It's 0300 on gate guard. Your eyelids weigh a hundred pounds and the coffee ran out an hour ago. What do you do?
You stayed alert all shift. Your relief found you sweaty but awake.
Rest your eyes for a sec
You dozed for ten minutes and nobody checked. Lucky.
The sergeant of the guard caught you asleep. NJP. Sleeping on post is no joke.
You and {buddy} talked about cars until sunrise.
The OD heard you tying up the net. Chewed out.
Your first real paycheck hit the account. It feels like a fortune. {buddy} says a dealership outside the gate has "military specials." What now?
You signed for a 24% APR Mustang. It is gorgeous. You are broke.
You squirreled it away. Future you says thanks.
Blow it all in one weekend
Strip club, steakhouse, tattoo. You don't remember Sunday.
A salesman outside the gate says your rank qualifies you for "zero down, easy payments" on a lifted truck. The fine print is tiny. What do you do?
The truck is sick. The 29% interest rate is sicker.
You spotted three hidden fees and walked out. The salesman cursed in two languages.
JAG told you it was a scam. You bought a used Corolla instead.
It's PT test day. You partied last night and your stomach is doing backflips. The run starts in five minutes. What's the plan?
You puked at the finish line but still maxed the run.
You failed the run by eight seconds. Remedial PT it is.
The medic gave you a profile and Motrin. Test rescheduled.
The medic saw right through you. Your squad leader is unimpressed.
Heart racing, you set a personal record.
Heart palpitations at mile one. You walked the rest.
Your squad leader needs "a volunteer" to help a colonel's spouse move furniture on Saturday. Everyone stares at you. What do you say?
You moved a piano up three flights. The spouse gave you cookies.
It worked. Somebody else got the piano.
They checked. You now get the piano AND Sunday detail.
You pointed at {buddy}. {buddy} will remember this.
Surprise room inspection in ten minutes. Your room smells like dip spit and old pizza. What do you do?
You shoved everything in your truck. Room passed.
They opened the wall locker. An avalanche of laundry.
Spray a whole can of Febreze
The inspector sniffed, coughed, and moved on.
It smells like a pizza in a meadow. Failed.
You failed. Weekend re-inspection for the whole floor. Everyone hates you.
You still have nightmares about your basic training instructor screaming about your "Gumby arms." Someone yells nearby and you flinch. How do you cope?
You told the story at chow. Everyone had their own.
You snapped to parade rest in a Walmart. A cashier was confused.
You're up to six energy drinks a day. Your hands shake when you shave. {buddy} is worried. What do you do?
Three days of headaches, then you felt human again.
You lasted 14 hours before raiding the shoppette.
You are vibrating at a frequency only dogs can hear.
Day four of a field exercise. It hasn't stopped raining, your socks are soup, and your poncho has a hole. What do you do?
Dry socks. The greatest luxury known to man.
Trench foot is starting but your team leader respects the grit.
You slept in the cab like royalty.
The platoon sergeant was already sleeping there. Bad move.
Your squad is trading MREs. You got Veggie Omelet, the worst one. {buddy} has Chili Mac. Make a deal?
{buddy} laughed in your face. Enjoy the omelet.
It tasted like a sponge soaked in regret.
You swapped bags while {buddy} wasn't looking.
{buddy} caught you. Now nobody trades with you.
You fell asleep standing up during a long safety brief and started tipping over. The first sergeant is watching. What now?
He did not buy it. Front leaning rest, move.
You admitted it. Extra duty, but he respected the honesty.
There's a party in the barracks. Someone brought a handle of vodka and a fog machine. The staff duty NCO is two floors down. Join in?
Legendary night. You woke up in the laundry room.
Staff duty walked in mid-keg-stand. Everyone got NJP.
You played video games and heard sirens later. Good call.
You drove three drunks home. You're a hero.
You've had five beers off base. It's ten minutes back to the gate. A rideshare costs $40. What do you do?
You made it back. Your hands were shaking all night.
Gate guards smelled it instantly. DUI, demotion, and a career on life support.
{buddy} grumbled but came. You owe them big.
You woke up in {country} with a fresh tattoo of a cartoon frog on your neck. Is that within regs?
The sergeant major noticed. Paperwork followed.
Painful and expensive. The frog is fading.
You named him Gerald. He's part of the team now.
A senior NCO stops you on the sidewalk. Your hands are in your pockets and you're on the phone. What do you do?
Twenty minutes of yelling. Your phone call ended long ago.
You walked away. Somehow, it worked.
He followed you to your unit. Your squad leader got involved.
Your first day at sea and the ship is rolling hard. You're greener than your uniform. What do you do?
It helped. Your stomach found its sea legs.
You puked over the rail. Into the wind. Onto yourself.
The old salts swear by it. It sort of worked.
Your chief dragged you out to swab the deck you puked on.
The ship just docked in {country}. You have 12 hours of liberty and a buddy pair with {buddy}. What's the plan?
Great night. You learned some local swear words.
Ancient ruins and street food. You sent photos home.
Twelve hours of glorious rack time.
FOD walk on the flight line at 0600. You spot a tiny bolt near a jet intake. Nobody else saw it. What do you do?
Pick it up and report it
Turns out it came off a tow bar. You may have saved a $30 million engine.
An engine ate the bolt. The investigation traced it to your lane.
Your recruiter promised you'd be "basically a pilot." You're cleaning latrines. What do you do?
Everyone starts somewhere. Your latrines sparkle.
You started prepping to reclassify. Smart.
Senior members of your unit say new guys have to "earn their spot" with a humiliating ritual tonight. What do you do?
Degrading, but it's over. They treat you like one of them now.
It got out of hand. You ended up at the clinic.
An investigation was opened. Some people won't talk to you now.
They called you soft but left you alone.
Your Kevlar is missing from your locker. Hand receipt check is tomorrow and it costs $500. What do you do?
It had a name written inside. You got NJP for larceny.
Buy one at the surplus store
You've been sneaking a fellow junior enlisted from another company into your room. The rules say no overnight guests. Keep it up?
Love wins. Staff duty never caught on.
Caught at 0500. Extra duty for both of you.
You moved out. Romantic, and expensive.
You called it off. Awkward at the chow hall now.
Mail call. Your high school sweetheart sent a letter. It starts with "I need to tell you something..." What do you do?
They're marrying your cousin. You stared at the wall for hours.
It was bad news. {buddy} bought you a pizza and roasted your ex.
Qualification day at the range. You're borderline and the wind is gusting. What's your approach?
You shot expert. Badge on the chest.
You missed qualifying by one. Back to the range.
Your team leader hands you $20 and says, "Get me a pack of smokes, a dip, and a Rip It. Keep the change." There's no change. Go?
You paid the rest. Team leader owes you one.
He gave you another five and a dirty look.
You're short on rent for your off-base apartment. A payday lender near the gate offers instant cash at "low" rates. What do you do?
You paid rent. The 300% APR will haunt you.
Interest-free loan from military relief. Lifesaver.
A scrawny stray dog keeps following your squad around base. Pets are banned in the barracks. What do you do?
You named it Private Biscuit. Morale is through the roof.
Animal control took Biscuit. Paperwork for you.
Biscuit found a family. You visit sometimes.
The dog likes the jalapeno cheese more than you do.
{buddy} skipped their guard shift and asks you to tell the sergeant they were there. What do you say?
The sergeant believed you. {buddy} owes you forever.
Caught lying on an official statement. You both got NJP.
You told the truth. {buddy} stopped talking to you.
You took a cool selfie in front of a classified screen and almost hit "post." What do you do?
It got 40 likes and nobody noticed. Dumb luck.
Security found it within an hour. Court-martial for mishandling classified info.
You deleted it and sweated for a week.
A reflection in your sunglasses showed the screen. NJP.
CBRN training. You're in the gas chamber and the instructor tells you to take off your mask and recite your social. What do you do?
Snot everywhere, but you stayed calm. Respect earned.
You bolted. The instructors made you go back in.
Twelve miles into a ruck march, your heel feels like it's on fire. You're near the back. What do you do?
You finished. Your sock is stuck to your foot with blood.
Your foot gave out. You rode in the sag wagon.
Thirty seconds of moleskin. You finished strong.
A guy in the barracks offers you synthetic weed and swears "it doesn't show up on a piss test." What do you do?
You felt weird for a day. Never again.
Random urinalysis caught it. You're being separated.
Two weeks later he got caught. Good call.
CID raided his room. Some people call you a snitch.
You just saluted a warrant officer's cousin who's wearing civilian clothes. Then you failed to salute an actual officer. What now?
You caught up and saluted. The officer laughed.
The officer chewed you out in front of the PX.
You set your rifle down for one second in the field and now it's gone. The whole battalion is about to halt. What do you do?
Your sergeant found it 30 feet away. You'll carry a broomstick for a month.
Found it under a bush. Nobody knows.
You waited too long. The whole battalion searched. NJP.
Your knee hurts a little. {buddy} says go to sick call to skip the ruck march. Do it?
You got a light-duty profile. Easy week.
Medic said walk it off. Now they call you "Sick Call Ranger."
You finished. Knee is angry, but you earned respect.
A fishing boat capsized in rough seas. Your crew is first on scene and a man is drowning 30 meters out. What do you do?
Perfect throw. You hauled him in.
The wind carried it off. A helicopter got him, barely.
You pulled him out against the swell. Commendation incoming.
The surf hammered you. You barely made it back.
Your new roommate never showers, plays drums at 2 AM, and eats your food. What do you do?
He agreed to shower. Small victories.
He shrugged and started drumming again.
He got moved. Peace at last.
He got the message. He showers now.
He reported it. You got NJP for assault.
The unit ball is this weekend. You have no date and the grog bowl looks suspicious. What do you do?
It contained Tabasco, rum, and a boot. You loved it.
You two danced to Cotton Eye Joe. Legendary.
Your first sergeant noticed. Mandatory fun is mandatory.
The career counselor waves a $20,000 re-enlistment bonus at you. Your contract ends in eight months. Sign?
You re-upped. Time to buy a boat you don't need.
You're weighing the GI Bill against the cash.
Counting days. Civilian life is calling.
You woke up at 0640. Formation was at 0630. Your phone shows 17 missed calls. What do you do?
You showed up with toothpaste on your face. Counseling statement.
They bought it and sent you to sick call.
Your squad leader saw your bar tab from last night on Instagram.
You're driving a truck in a convoy at night on blackout drive. The NVGs are fogging up and the road is narrow. What's your move?
You kept your interval. The convoy arrived safe.
You fell behind and got lost for 20 minutes.
Smooth driving. Your truck commander was impressed.
You rolled into a ditch. Truck on its side, bruised ribs.
Someone burned popcorn and the barracks fire alarm is going off at 0200. Everyone has to stand outside in the cold. You know who did it. Say?
The microwave was confiscated from the whole floor.
You froze for an hour. Solidarity.
The gym on base is free and open 24/7. {buddy} wants to start a bulking program together. In?
Six weeks later, your sleeves are tight.
Sketchy pre-workout gave you heart palpitations.
You maxed a different kind of level.
Money keeps disappearing from rooms. You catch a guy from your squad walking out of a neighbor's room with a wallet. What do you do?
He returned it and confessed to the chain of command.
He swung at you and ran.
He was caught and kicked out.
{rank} {name}, your platoon sergeant is screaming at you inches from your face because your boots aren't shined. How do you react?
You let it wash over you. It ended eventually.
Mistake. Push-ups until your arms gave up.
Textbook response. He walked off satisfied.
One of your junior soldiers has been late three times this week and smells like booze. He looks exhausted. How do you handle it?
He admitted his marriage is falling apart. You got him to chaplain support.
Smoke him in front of everyone
He's sore and humiliated. The real problem remains.
Send him to the ASAP program
Substance abuse counseling. He thanked you a year later.
Your evaluation is due and your rater wrote "solid performer." In promotion-speak, that's a death sentence. What do you do?
You got "Most Qualified" with strong bullets.
Your rater got defensive. Eval unchanged.
Promotion just got a lot harder.
Your rater copied them word for word.
You're in front of the promotion board. The sergeant major asks you to recite the NCO Creed. Your mind goes blank. What do you do?
You nailed it. Selected for promotion.
You stumbled on the second paragraph. Not selected this time.
They appreciated the honesty and your other answers carried you.
You're leading a 12-mile ruck. One of your soldiers is falling way behind and crying. How do you handle it?
You took his radio. The whole squad finished together.
He collapsed. Heat casualty. Investigation pending.
Drop him to the sag wagon
He's safe, but squad pride took a hit.
It's 0300. Off-post police call: one of your soldiers was arrested for fighting outside a club. What do you do?
You bailed him out and got the story. He was defending a friend.
A night in jail taught him something.
The first sergeant had to go. He was not pleased with you.
A young soldier has been giving away his gear and says "it won't matter soon." What do you do?
You asked. He admitted it. You walked him to behavioral health. He's alive.
He was escorted to help. You check on him daily.
He was okay. You still feel uneasy.
He took his own life two days later. You will carry this forever.
You're staff duty NCO and hear music and laughter coming from a room after quiet hours. Smells like weed. What do you do?
Three soldiers with a vape full of THC. You did your job.
Turn down the music and leave
You avoided the drama. For now.
They hauled them off. The commander is pleased.
A new private with a lot of potential asks you how to make sergeant fast. What advice do you give?
Two years later, he pinned sergeant and thanked you.
You have to teach a class to your squad on land navigation. Half of them are falling asleep. What do you do?
Hands-on with a real map. Everyone learned something.
Winners got a day off. Suddenly everyone loves land nav.
Inventory is due. You're missing two night vision devices worth $8,000 each. Someone suggests "adjusting" the paperwork. What do you do?
Investigation found them in another unit's connex. Close call.
An audit caught it. Court-martial for false official records.
One of your soldiers tells you she's pregnant and scared to tell the chain of command. What do you do?
You helped her get the right profile and resources.
Word got around. She filed an EO complaint.
Your new lieutenant insists the platoon walk the wrong direction on a land nav exercise. He's confident. You know he's wrong. What do you do?
He listened. Crisis averted. He trusts you now.
Three hours lost. He learned. So did the company commander.
The platoon loved it. He didn't.
You're at the NCO academy. You could aim for the Commandant's List but it means no sleep. Worth it?
Commandant's List. Your career just accelerated.
You burned out and finished middle of the pack.
Graduated. You slept eight hours a night.
One of your married soldiers shows up with scratches on his face. He says "it's nothing." What do you do?
He opened up. You connected him and his spouse with the family advocacy program.
Things got worse. MPs got involved two weeks later.
Finance shorted one of your soldiers $1,500 and he can't pay rent. Finance says "two to three pay periods." What do you do?
You camped there until it got fixed. Hero to your soldier.
The finance clerk took your yelling personally. Even slower now.
He paid you back. You built serious loyalty.
Tell him to suck it up
He got evicted. Morale in the squad dropped.
You've developed feelings for a private in your own platoon. They seem to feel the same. What do you do?
Nobody found out. You're walking a razor's edge.
Someone saw you holding hands. Fraternization. Busted down a rank.
You moved units. Now it's legal. Mostly.
The right call. It still stings.
You're range safety. A private turns around with a loaded weapon pointing down the firing line. What do you do?
Everyone froze. You redirected the barrel. Nobody died today.
You took him down safely. Weapon pointed downrange.
A round went off into the dirt and grazed your leg.
Your best specialist has the soldier of the quarter board tomorrow. He's nervous. Do you help?
He won. Your squad has bragging rights.
He bombed. The other squad leader smirked.
Monday morning. Your whole squad is visibly hungover after a three-day weekend. PT is about to start. What do you do?
Ninety minutes of burpees. Lesson learned.
They appreciated the mercy. Loyalty earned.
Aboard ship, you discover a junior sailor has been brewing the chief's mess coffee with week-old grounds. The chiefs are furious. Cover for him?
The chiefs hazed you a bit. Your sailor will die for you now.
He scrubbed the coffee urn with a toothbrush.
You're inspecting dress uniforms. One soldier has his ribbons upside down and a missing badge. Inspection is in an hour. What do you do?
Ten minutes with a ruler. Passed.
Your family's base housing has black mold in the bathroom. Your kid has been coughing. Privatized housing says it's "a cosmetic issue." What do you do?
They moved you to a new unit within a week.
They painted over it. Your kid still coughs.
The story aired. Repairs started the next day.
The garrison commander was not happy with you.
Before a field exercise, you find a private's ruck is stuffed with pillows to look full. What do you do?
Make him carry a sandbag too
Your squad thinks you're cool. The first sergeant doesn't.
A soldier tells you another NCO has been sending her inappropriate messages. The NCO is your friend. What do you do?
An investigation opened. Doing the right thing cost you a friendship.
He denied it and deleted everything.
One of your soldiers failed tape test again. One more and he's chaptered out. He really wants to stay. What do you do?
Rules are rules. He went home.
The command sergeant major spotted your soldiers walking on the grass. He wants to see you in his office. What do you say?
You made the cut-off score for promotion. The pinning ceremony is Friday and your family wants to come. Hold a party?
Promotion pinned. Brisket smoked. Life is good.
Pinned on the motor pool floor. Humble.
Your crew is rushing an aircraft for launch. A junior airman skipped a torque check to save time. Launch is in 10 minutes. What do you do?
You found a loose panel. Maintenance officer quietly thanked you.
A panel tore off in flight. Safety investigation names you.
Your unit got orders. You deploy to {country} in 60 days. Your spouse just found out. How do you break it?
Tears, but you made a plan together.
Not your finest moment. It led to a fight.
You got rear detachment. Your spouse is relieved.
Denied. And your first sergeant thinks you're soft.
The battalion is holding a PT competition. Your squad can win a four-day pass. What's your strategy?
He pulled a hamstring on day one.
Your shop smells like death. A raccoon died in the ventilation system. Maintenance says six weeks. What do you do?
You removed it. You will never smell normal again.
Order the junior troops to do it
Done. A private threw up twice.
You're detailed as a casualty notification NCO. You have to knock on a family's door to tell them their son died. How do you prepare?
You did it with dignity. You cried in the car afterward.
The mother screamed. You will hear it forever.
Your senior NCO wants to smoke the platoon for a minor mistake. You think it's pointless. Speak up?
He agreed to a retraining instead.
The platoon suffered. Nobody learned anything.
Your spouse got into a feud with the first sergeant's spouse at the family readiness group. Now it's affecting work. What do you do?
It blew over in three months. Very long months.
You slept on the couch for a week.
You've been selected for drill sergeant or recruiter duty. Both are brutal but career-enhancing. Which?
You got the hat. You now yell for a living.
Strip mall office, quotas, and lies. Welcome to recruiting.
A real person-overboard alarm sounds at night. You're the senior petty officer on deck. What do you do?
Run the drill by the book
Life ring thrown, spotters out, sailor recovered in nine minutes.
You got them. Reckless, but it worked.
The swells nearly took you too.
Your best soldier wants to get out. The command wants retention numbers. He asks for honest advice. What do you say?
He got out, went to college, and still texts you.
He re-upped. You hope he doesn't regret it.
Your platoon has been walking for two hours. You're pretty sure the objective is north. Your platoon sergeant is giving you a look. What do you do?
He pointed the right way. Ego bruised, mission saved.
You were right! Shock in the platoon.
You led them to a cow pasture. The story will follow you forever.
The battalion commander wants a 50-slide brief on vehicle maintenance by 0700. It's 2200. What do you do?
Every slide perfect. The commander said "good." Just "good."
Nobody noticed the dates. Asleep by 2300.
Slide 12 still had the old unit's name on it.
Officer evaluation reports are due. Your rater is a micromanager who hasn't seen half your work. What do you do?
He used it almost verbatim. Top block.
You're a brand new platoon leader. Thirty soldiers are sizing you up. Your first speech?
"I'm here to learn and lead." They respected it.
They laughed. At you, not with you.
You took command of a company. Morale is low, and there's a problem first sergeant. Where do you start?
You found common ground. The company is turning around.
He undermines you at every turn.
Cookouts, recognition, fair duty roster. Morale climbing.
The inspector general team arrives Monday to inspect your unit. Your arms room records are a mess. What do you do?
Passed with zero findings. Nobody saw their family for 48 hours.
They didn't look at the arms room. Miracle.
Massive findings. The colonel wants a word.
Your company lost $40,000 of gear during a field exercise. As commander, you're financially liable if negligence is found. What do you do?
It was a theft, not negligence. You're cleared.
The investigating officer saw through it. Relieved of command.
You're a new second lieutenant walking past 200 soldiers outside the PX. Your arm is getting tired from saluting. What do you do?
You walked behind the dumpsters. Smart.
A crusty sergeant first class "accidentally" calls you "Ensign" and "Kid" in front of the platoon. How do you respond?
He grinned. You earned a sliver of respect.
You won the battle. Not the war.
You're briefing the brigade commander. Halfway in, the projector dies. All eyes are on you. What do you do?
Calm and clear. "That's how you brief," the colonel said.
You blanked on the key numbers.
You're attracted to a sergeant in your chain of command. They flirt back at the unit ball. What do you do?
Career intact. Heart a bit sad.
It came out in an investigation. You resigned your commission.
Battalion piled four new taskings onto your training calendar this week. Your soldiers are exhausted. What do you do?
Two taskings got moved. The troops noticed.
After a field exercise, your company is short one rifle. Nobody leaves until it's found. It's 2100 Friday. What do you do?
Found it in a truck bed at 0100.
Search went into Sunday. Brigade got involved.
Your troops won't forget that you left.
A soldier reports being assaulted by a popular team leader. The team leader's squad is pressuring the victim. What do you do?
You separated them and stopped the retaliation. The case moved forward.
The victim felt abandoned and requested a transfer.
You're a new division officer aboard ship. Your chief says, "Sir, let me handle the sailors. You handle the paperwork." How do you respond?
Best advice you ever got. Your division runs smoothly.
Your flight instructor says you're on the edge of washing out of flight school. One more checkride. How do you prepare?
You passed. Wings are within reach.
Washed out. You'll be a logistics officer now.
You've been moved to battalion staff. Your job is now spreadsheets and meetings about meetings. How do you cope?
You automated half your job. The XO thinks you're a genius.
Request to go back to the line
A defense contractor offers you a "free" Super Bowl trip after you approve their vendor bid. What do you do?
Ethics counselor thanked you. Contractor got flagged.
IG investigation. Charged with accepting gratuities and forced out.
Your platoon is pinned down by machine gun fire from a tree line in {country}. Your radio operator is waiting for orders. What do you do?
Artillery silenced the gun. Nobody lost.
Danger close. Fragments hit you. Medevac.
You flanked and took the position. Bronze Star with V.
A round hit you in the hip as you crossed open ground.
Everyone made it out. Mission incomplete.
You've worked 80-hour weeks for months. Your spouse says, "I feel like a single parent." What do you do?
A week at the beach. Your family remembered who you are.
Later never came. Couples counseling is next.
You have a slot for air assault school. It's famous for brutal ruck marches and rappelling off helicopters. Go?
You earned the wings. Your platoon respects you more.
Failed the 12-mile ruck by two minutes.
Pass the slot to a sergeant
He graduated. He'll remember your gesture.
You're planning a company morale event. Budget: $0. Expectations: high. What do you do?
Fifteen chilis. One hospitalization. Great success.
Nothing says morale like running at 0530.
A soldier in your company was killed in a training accident. The investigation is examining your safety procedures. How do you handle it?
You were cleared. You still think about it every day.
Relieved for loss of confidence. Your career is likely over.
Cleared. But people noticed you got defensive.
You're liberty officer for a port visit to {country}. 400 sailors. You must keep them out of jail. Strategy?
Zero incidents. A miracle at sea.
A sailor tried to steal a horse. International incident.
You're at the career course. Your study group wants to copy last year's answers. What do you do?
The instructor noticed. Honor code violation.
It's September. Your battalion must spend $2 million in two weeks or lose it next year. What do you buy?
The soldiers love it. Morale up.
Fiscally honorable. The brigade commander thinks you're crazy.
A member of Congress is touring your installation tomorrow. The barracks have mold and broken AC. What do you show them?
Funding approved for renovation within a year.
The general is furious you embarrassed the command.
A national reporter asks you about a recent training accident on camera. Public affairs is sweating. What do you say?
Clip went viral for the right reasons.
One sentence was taken out of context.
The two-star wants your brigade to pilot a new "Wellness Initiative" with 47 mandatory briefings. Your soldiers are drowning in requirements. What do you do?
The general is pleased. Your troops are not.
The general trimmed it to 10 briefings. You're a hero.
The general called you "not a team player." Ouch.
The centralized selection list is out. Your name is on it as an alternate. What do you do?
A principal declined. You're in command.
Someone made a call. You're in.
A command climate survey shows one of your battalion commanders is toxic. He's also your best tactician. What do you do?
Hard call. The battalion's climate improved fast.
A soldier's suicide note named him. Now it's on you.
A major hurricane hit the coast. You've been put in charge of joint relief operations. Roads are flooded and communications are down. Priorities?
Your helicopters pulled 300 people off rooftops.
Once comms came up, everything got faster.
Precious hours lost. Criticism in the news.
You have 26 years in. A defense contractor offers you triple your salary to retire and consult. What do you do?
Retired with honors. Now you sell drones to your old friends.
You're going for general. Family sighs.
A foreign general from {country} is visiting and serves you a local delicacy: fermented sheep eye. Everyone watches. What do you do?
Awkward. The partnership stalled for a week.
Your staff's classified briefing just appeared on a gaming chat server. The press is calling. What's your move?
It was a junior analyst trying to win an argument. Contained.
Congress demanded answers. Your career took a hit.
You've been assigned to the Pentagon. Long hours, no troops, endless staff work. How do you approach it?
You met all the right people. Stars may be in your future.
Your installation has lost four soldiers to suicide in two months. What do you do?
Embedded counselors, no-stigma policies. Numbers improved.
Your file is in front of the general officer selection board. One black mark from a decade ago. What do you do?
Not selected. Your career may have peaked.
Write a letter to the board
It drew more attention to the issue.
Your convoy is rolling through {country} when the lead vehicle stops. Something looks off in the road ahead. What do you do?
EOD found a pressure plate IED. Patience saved lives.
A secondary device detonated under your vehicle.
The base sirens wail: "INCOMING!" You're in the shower, naked and soapy. What do you do?
You made it in a towel. Everyone has seen everything now.
Hit the deck where you are
Rounds landed 200 meters away. Back to the shower.
Shrapnel punched through the shower trailer.
Your patrol in {country} gets ambushed. Rounds are cracking overhead and {buddy} is down in the open. What do you do?
You pulled {buddy} behind a wall under fire. Bronze Star.
killed rescuing a buddy under fire
Your fire suppressed them. A medic got to {buddy}.
You couldn't move. Someone else saved {buddy}. You can't forgive yourself.
A grenade bounces into the room where your squad is taking cover. There's no time. What do you do?
Your body armor absorbed most of it. You survived. Medal of Honor.
killed smothering a grenade to save the squad
You saved everyone in that room.
It went off at the doorway.
A single shot cracks past your head on an observation post. A sniper is somewhere in the buildings. What do you do?
Air support handled the building. You're shaken but alive.
You spotted the glint. Called it in. Threat eliminated.
A soldier is bleeding out on a dusty field. The medevac is 30 minutes away. You're the closest one with a tourniquet. What do you do?
You stopped the bleed. He made it to surgery.
You did everything right. He didn't make it.
The medic got there. It was close.
Since returning from {country}, you wake up drenched in sweat, hearing explosions. Fireworks make you hit the ground. What do you do?
{buddy} has the same dreams. You're not alone.
Your back, knees, and hearing are shot. The VA claim process is 80 pages long. What do you do?
A Veterans Service Officer got you a fair rating.
"Other people need it more." Your knees disagree.
After nine months in {country}, your plane lands. Your family is in the gym waiting with signs. How do you feel?
Hugs, tears, and your dog lost its mind.
It's a lot. Readjusting will take time.
You got orders to a new duty station across the country. The movers broke your TV and lost a box. What do you do?
Do a DITY move next time
You moved yourself and pocketed the difference.
Between deployments and field time, you've been home 90 days this year. Your spouse says they're exhausted. What do you do?
The chaplain-run retreat helped more than you expected.
They moved back to their parents' place.
A long, hard conversation. You're okay.
Your unit is deployed to help after a massive earthquake in {country}. A child is trapped under rubble. What do you do?
You pulled her out alive. Her mother kissed your hands.
An aftershock collapsed more rubble. You were too late.
The crane arrived. She survived, barely.
You're eligible for the GI Bill. College, trade school, or transfer it to your kid?
Tuition paid plus a housing stipend.
Your kid will go to college debt-free.
You get a care package from an elementary school class. Crayon drawings and beef jerky. What do you do?
They framed your letter in the classroom.
Your ears have been ringing for a week after a live-fire exercise without proper protection. What do you do?
Mild damage documented. Good for future VA claims.
"What?" You say that a lot now.
Rockets are hitting the base in {country}. You're crossing open ground near the motor pool. What do you do?
Dirt in your teeth, but alive.
{buddy} was killed by a roadside bomb this morning. The memorial is tomorrow. How do you deal with it?
You told the funny stories. Everyone laughed and cried.
You haven't cried. You haven't slept either.
It didn't fix anything. But it helped.
A stray cat has adopted your outpost in {country}. General Order No. 1 prohibits pets. Keep it?
Sergeant Whiskers keeps the rats away. Morale soars.
The command sergeant major found Whiskers.
Through a nonprofit, Whiskers now lives with your family.
You've been assigned to burn pit duty. The black smoke smells like plastic and death. No respirator available. What do you do?
You coughed for a month. Hope it doesn't catch up later.
Your cutter intercepts a semi-submersible full of cocaine. The smugglers are scrambling to scuttle it. What do you do?
It sank fast. You barely got off it.
Crew detained. Most of the drugs sank, but nobody died.
You're monitoring satellite feeds and see a convoy forming near friendly troops. It might be civilians. What do you report?
Report what you see, no guess
Command got more eyes on it. Civilians. A bad call avoided.
It was a wedding party. You think about it constantly.
Base housing has a waiting list of six months. A friend says he knows "a guy" who can bump you up for $500. What do you do?
The guy was a scammer. And you're now in an investigation.
Six months in a budget hotel. You hate it.
A typhoon is battering the ship. Waves are crashing over the bow and something is loose on deck. What do you do?
Tethered and secured. Chief nodded at you.
A wave slammed you into a bulkhead.
It broke loose and smashed a radar mast.
The interpreter who saved your life in {country} is now being hunted. He emails you for a visa recommendation. What do you do?
He got a visa. You picked him up from the airport.
You never heard from him again.
In a bar in {country}, a local starts a fight with {buddy}. The local police are already nearby. What do you do?
You dragged {buddy} out the back door. International incident avoided.
During a live-fire exercise, you notice a vehicle has wandered onto the bombing range. Jets are inbound. What do you do?
Strike aborted. A lost farmer. You saved his life.
Tragedy. You will relive it forever.
Your back injury is getting worse. The doctor recommends a medical board, which could end your career. What do you do?
You're still in. But at what cost?
A massive wildfire is threatening a town near base. The governor requests military help. You volunteer. What do you do?
Exhausting work. The town was saved.
You carried an elderly man to safety. He cried.
The dining facility is serving something labeled "Meat." Just "Meat." You're starving. Eat it?
Surprisingly decent. You still don't know what it was.
Food poisoning. Two days on the toilet.
Iceberg lettuce and ranch. Living the dream.
Night watch in an old building on base. You hear footsteps on the floor above. It's supposed to be empty. What do you do?
It was a raccoon. You screamed louder than it did.
Nothing there. But the door you locked is now open.
You find out someone has been recording people in the shower trailers. You know who it is. What do you do?
He attacked you and destroyed the evidence.
A stranger at a restaurant thanks you for your service and wants to pay for your meal. What do you do?
Nice gesture. You tipped the waitress extra.
A fellow service member is posting heated political rants in uniform on social media. What do you do?
Your unit lost radio contact with higher in {country}. You're the only one who knows the backup satellite system. What do you do?
Comms restored in four minutes. They called you a wizard.
The battery was dead. Nobody charged it.
You need new boots. The issue ones gave you blisters. The PX sells $250 boots that are actually comfortable. Buy?
Your feet thank you every single day.
Your hometown newspaper wants to do a story about your service. Your old high school bully reads it. What do you say in the interview?
Classy article. Your mom framed it.
You might have implied you were a Navy SEAL. You were not.
Day 4 of SFAS. Your heels look like raw hamburger and the next ruck is 12 miles with 55 lbs. What will you do?
You finish inside the time standard. The cadre write something down. You choose to believe it was good.
You hobble in late. The cadre write something down. It was not good.
The medic drains them and shrugs. 'Your call, candidate.' You lose a little time but keep your feet.
You sign the voluntary withdrawal form. The ride back is very quiet.
Solo land navigation at Camp Mackall, night, no lights. Your points are across a swamp nobody wants to cross. What will you do?
Waist-deep and miserable, but you hit every point with time to spare.
You lose your pace count in the muck and wander until sunrise.
Slow but solid. You hit your points with minutes left.
You're too slow and miss one point.
Nobody sees you. You feel guilty and fast.
A cadre truck is parked right there, lights off. Road walking is an instant problem.
Team Week. Six candidates, one telephone pole, and a cadre who says the log 'looks lonely.' {buddy} is visibly slacking. What will you do?
Your shoulders scream, but the peers notice who carried the load.
{buddy} picks it up. Nobody likes you, but the log moves.
Arguing under a log goes badly. The cadre love it. You don't.
Peer evals are brutal. Everyone noticed.
Cadre hand you a sheet: rank your team from best to worst. {buddy} has carried you all week but has a big ego. What will you do?
You rate {buddy} near the top. Honesty is what they're actually grading.
It works. You feel gross about it.
Everyone else rated {buddy} first. The cadre notice the outlier: you.
The Nasty Nick obstacle course. The rope over the water is slick and your grip is gone. What will you do?
You hang on by pure spite and make it across.
Splash. The cadre call you 'Aquaman' for a week.
Leg lock, slow and steady. Boring and effective.
Technique isn't enough with noodle arms. You fall.
Rucking alone at 0300, a cadre truck stops. 'Rough night? Hop in, warm cab, hot coffee.' What will you do?
You say 'No thanks, sergeant' and keep moving. The truck pulls off. That was the test.
The coffee is great. Your SFAS career is over.
Final formation at SFAS. They read names for 'selected.' Yours is called. {buddy}'s isn't. What will you do?
You tell {buddy} to come back next year. {buddy} swears they will.
You whoop in the formation. Half the room glares.
SERE resistance lab. An 'interrogator' slaps the table and demands your unit's mission. You're cold, hungry, and very tired. What will you do?
Name, rank, service number. The instructors debrief you as a solid resister.
You crack and give a believable cover story with real details. The debrief is awkward.
Your sarcasm somehow works on their nerves. Barely.
Mouthing off earns you a lot more stress positions.
The Army assigned you a language for the Q Course. The instructor talks fast and your test is Friday. What will you do?
You pass with a solid score. You start dreaming in verb conjugations.
You study hard and still fail the oral. Recycle.
You make friends at a local restaurant and your speaking takes off.
You mostly learn slang you can't use on the test.
Somehow you pass. Nobody knows how.
You fail. The team sergeant's face says it all.
18B training: strip and reassemble a foreign machine gun blindfolded, against the clock. What will you do?
You beat the class record. Instructors start calling you 'Hands.'
A spring launches into the dark. You find it after time expires.
Clean pass. Slow is smooth, smooth is fast.
18C class. You must calculate a cutting charge for a steel beam. Your numbers look off. What will you do?
You find your decimal error. The beam drops perfectly.
Still wrong. The instructor sighs and shows you.
Huge boom. The beam is gone. So is a nearby port-a-john.
Shrapnel dents a range truck. Safety violation. Article 15.
18D trauma lane: a screaming simulated casualty, arterial bleed, airway compromised, 3 minutes. What will you do?
Bleed controlled, airway secured. Your instructor nods once, which is huge.
You tighten it too slowly. 'Your patient bled out.'
You get lucky. The instructor lectures you on MARCH anyway.
Wrong order. The patient 'dies.' You hear about it all week.
18E commo training. Morse at 13 words per minute. Everything sounds like a cricket being angry. What will you do?
You start hearing words in the beeps. You pass.
Your brain melts and you fail the timed test.
Weird rhymes stick in your head. Good enough.
Robin Sage, North Carolina. A real local farmer playing a 'G-chief' supporter offers his barn and a pot roast. What will you do?
Best meal in weeks. You build rapport, which is the whole point.
Tactically sound, emotionally devastating. The pot roast haunts you.
Robin Sage. The role-player guerrilla chief demands your team give his fighters your rifles before he'll cooperate. What will you do?
You trade training for trust. The cadre grade you well on rapport.
He storms off. Your detachment loses a day.
He 'kicks you out of Pineland.' Not great.
Airborne School, first jump. The door opens and the ground looks very far away. What will you do?
Your chute opens. You yell something embarrassing. You're hooked.
Bad landing. You roll your ankle hard.
A jumpmaster gently but firmly removes you from the door and your training.
Military Free Fall school in Yuma. Your first jump from altitude. You go unstable and start spinning. What will you do?
You recover, hit your altitude, and pull clean. Instructors give a thumbs up.
You pull while spinning and get a line twist. Hard landing, sore back.
Safe, but you get chewed out for pulling high.
Your canopy opens into a mess of lines. You cut away and land on your reserve, shaken.
Combat Diver qualification. Instructors rip your mask and tie your hoses in knots underwater. Lungs burning. What will you do?
You untangle every knot and keep your regulator. You pass the pool comp.
You bolt for the surface. Fail.
You live to try again someday. Not this class.
A cadre inspects rucks and finds three candy bars in yours. On a fasting day. What will you do?
'Mine, sergeant.' You do pushups until the candy is a distant memory.
The cadre believe you. {buddy} doesn't speak to you.
{buddy} has an alibi. You are now known as the snack snitch.
The cadre actually laughs. Takes one. Moves on.
Barracks fire watch at 0300 after three days of no sleep. Your eyes are closing on their own. What will you do?
You make it through the shift without incident.
You wake up seconds before the next guy shows. Close one.
The staff duty NCO finds you snoring. Article 15.
You see a candidate take {buddy}'s night vision cover. Gear is getting 'borrowed' everywhere. What will you do?
The gear is returned. {buddy} owes you.
{buddy} is squared away. Nobody asks questions.
Now you're the thief on camera. Article 15.
Saturday on Bragg Blvd. A drunk guy calls your beret 'a costume.' {buddy} is already rolling up sleeves. What will you do?
You drag {buddy} out. Your team sergeant would be proud, if bored.
Short fight. Cops arrive late. Nobody presses charges.
Military police, a black eye, and an Article 15.
0630 PT formation and you're still a little drunk from last night. The team sergeant is walking the line. What will you do?
You sweat out the tequila and survive the run.
You throw up during the run. In front of the colonel.
Sick call buys you a day. Nobody pushes.
Sick call doc writes 'alcohol' on the form. Oops.
Just finished the Q Course. A Fayetteville dealer offers you a muscle car at 24% APR, 'military discount.' What will you do?
It's loud, fast, and will cost you more than a house.
Boring. Smart. Your team sergeant approves.
The salesman yells 'thank you for your service' at your back.
You got your Long Tab. {buddy} wants matching tattoos of the SF crest tonight. What will you do?
Looks great. Your mom will hate it.
{buddy} gets it alone and calls you a coward for weeks.
First week on your ODA. The team sergeant says the team room is 'disgusting' and looks right at you. What will you do?
You scrub until it sparkles. The team grunts approval.
He laughs and assigns it to someone else. Lucky.
Wrong question. Now you clean the cage too.
{buddy} sends you to the supply cage to get a 'box of grid squares' for the land nav class. What will you do?
The supply sergeant laughs for five full minutes. You're officially initiated.
'Nice try.' {buddy} grins. You pass the vibe check.
First deployment to {country}. A partner soldier shoots with his eyes closed and holds the rifle sideways. What will you do?
By day's end, he's hitting the target. He brings you tea.
He nods, then keeps shooting sideways.
He stops showing up to training. Rapport: zero.
In {country}, village elders pour you endless sweet tea. You're full and need to pee badly. What will you do?
The elders are delighted. Your bladder is not.
An elder looks insulted. The vibe chills.
Training exercise at Camp Mackall. Your GPS died and the map is soaked. What will you do?
Hills and creeks get you home. Old school wins.
You wander into a different training lane. Embarrassing.
They find you. They also tell everyone.
Halfway through a Q Course field problem, your ankle rolls and pops loudly. What will you do?
You finish. Doc says it's sprained, not broken. Lucky.
It was broken. Now you're recycled for months.
X-ray, crutches, recycle. Painful but smart.
Q Course graduation. Your family flew in. You put on the green beret for the first time. What will you do?
Your dad tries not to cry and fails.
Big night out. Little memory of it.
Small Unit Tactics lane. You're squad leader and the 'enemy' is coming down the trail early. What will you do?
Clean kill zone. The evaluator gives you a GO.
Half the squad isn't in position. NO-GO.
You wait for the main body. Smart call.
There was no main body. NO-GO.
Your training cycle ends. The cadre want to recommend someone as honor graduate. You're in the running. What will you do?
You earn honor grad and a commendation.
You don't win, but three guys pass because of you.
In {country}, the partner force commander is collecting pay for 40 'soldiers' who don't exist. What will you do?
An investigation fixes the roster. The commander sulks but complies.
Nothing happens. The commander now hates you.
He admits it, fixes it, and respects you more.
He stops cooperating with your team.
The fighters you train go unpaid. Some quit.
A new partner recruit in {country} keeps staring at your team and asked when you all sleep. What will you do?
He's linked to insurgents. Your vigilance saves lives.
He's just weird. Partner leaders are offended.
Exhausting but safe. He deserts a week later.
He opens fire inside the wire.
Your 18D skills are needed. A woman in a {country} village is in a hard labor and the nearest hospital is 6 hours away. What will you do?
Mother and baby survive. The village names the baby after the team.
Complications you couldn't fix. You'll carry this one.
A helicopter takes her to a hospital in time.
Medevac is refused for a non-combat case.
Free clinic day in {country}. 400 people showed up and you have supplies for 150. What will you do?
You treat the sickest first. Hard choices, best outcome.
Fights break out in line. The village elder is not pleased.
An 18C task: the village in {country} needs a well. A local contractor wants twice the going rate. What will you do?
Your team digs it. Water flows. Kids cheer.
You hit rock. Project stalls for weeks.
The well gets built. Slow and expensive but done.
Your 18E gear dies mid-mission in {country}. Satellite link down, HF static, team needs contact. What will you do?
A wire, a tree, and math. You get through.
Static only. The team goes without comms overnight.
You walk out of the dead zone and reestablish.
Afghanistan. Your patrol takes PKM fire from the ridge. Partner forces scatter. {buddy} is pinned in the open. What will you do?
You drag {buddy} behind a wall under fire. Later, a Silver Star.
You're hit before you get there.
Your machine gun keeps their heads down. {buddy} crawls to cover.
A round finds you behind cover.
Mortars walk onto the ridge. Silence.
Too slow. {buddy} takes a round in the leg.
Syria. ISIS fighters hit your partner force's checkpoint at night. The partners are falling back. What will you do?
You lead from the front. The checkpoint holds. Bronze Star with V.
An AC-130 changes the conversation entirely.
Niger. Your vehicles are ambushed near a village by 50+ fighters. Comms are spotty. What will you do?
You bound back under fire. Everyone gets out.
killed in an ambush in the Sahel
French jets arrive at the last minute. You earned a Silver Star.
{buddy} is showing up hungover and shaky. The team sergeant hasn't noticed yet. What will you do?
{buddy} admits it and goes to treatment. You saved a career.
{buddy} tells you to mind your own business.
{buddy} goes to counseling, furious at you.
Nobody finds out. {buddy} gets better on their own.
It blows up on a range day. You're both in trouble.
Your newest junior guy lost a sensitive item: a night vision device. What will you do?
Found it in a truck. Lesson learned, quietly.
It's gone. Investigation, paperwork, angry colonel.
He'll never lose it again. He also hates you now.
Your new detachment commander wants to do a mission plan the team sergeant thinks is reckless. What will you do?
The captain adjusts the plan. Good partnership.
It goes badly. Minor injuries all round.
Night HALO infil into {country} from 25,000 ft. Your oxygen mask starts fogging at exit. What will you do?
You stack on your jumpmaster and land on target.
You miss the DZ and land in a tree.
You stay on the bird. Safe, but the team goes in one short.
Combat dive team. Night insertion off the {country} coast. Your rebreather is acting up. What will you do?
You swap and keep moving. Silent and on time.
You surface too quickly. Mild decompression issues.
Colombia. A man in a nice watch offers you $50,000 to tell him your partner unit's raid schedule. What will you do?
Counterintel thanks you. The man disappears from town.
You get away with it. You don't sleep well.
Philippines. A typhoon tears through your partner's island camp. Supplies are scattered and families are trapped. What will you do?
You pull families out of debris. The town remembers.
A wall collapses on your leg.
Weapons and radios are safe. The partners notice your priorities.
Philippines. Your partner Marines want you on a jungle raid against a militant camp. ROE says advise, not assault. What will you do?
You coordinate fires and ISR. Partners take the camp.
You shape the fight. Nobody upstairs complains.
Your commander finds out. Article 15 for violating ROE.
A young 18X is struggling and thinking about quitting. He reminds you of yourself. What will you do?
He quits. Maybe it wasn't for him. Maybe.
Your spouse says: 'One more deployment and I'm done.' Your team is leaving in two months. What will you do?
Your marriage stabilizes. Your team sergeant is disappointed.
You come home to an empty house.
Military family counseling actually helps. You deploy with her blessing.
Counseling turns into a lawyer meeting.
You keep waking up at 3 AM from the same dream about {country}. You're short-tempered and drinking more. What will you do?
It's hard, but it helps. You sleep through the night again.
The bottle makes the nights quieter and the days worse.
{buddy} has the same dream. You're not alone.
You're picked as SFAS cadre. A candidate who is clearly struggling looks you right in the eyes and asks for water. What will you do?
He's dehydrated. You may have saved his life.
Rules are rules. He drinks at the next checkpoint.
