Promotion board for Sergeant First Class. A sergeant major asks a trick question about counseling regs. What will you do?
You fumble. The board passes you over.
They respect the honesty. You're not promoted, though.
Your team spots a pressure-plate IED in {country}. EOD is three hours out. What will you do?
A clean controlled detonation. You move on.
You bypass it and mark for EOD.
There was a second IED on the bypass.
You captured a gold-plated AK from an insurgent leader in {country}. {buddy} says you could ship it home. What will you do?
It ends up in a museum display case at Bragg.
It hangs over your fireplace. Illegal and you know it.
Customs finds it. Article 15 and reduction in rank.
A partner soldier is shot through the thigh 50 meters away, still under fire. What will you do?
You drag him back and pack the wound. He lives. Bronze Star with V.
killed rescuing a wounded partner soldier
Under smoke, partners pull him in.
You see partner soldiers beating a detainee. They say 'this is how we do it here.' What will you do?
You step in. The beating stops. Report filed.
They stop, then do it when you're gone.
US aid to that unit is paused. They're furious, but it's the law.
Sniper overwatch over a {country} compound. A man emerges with something long in his hands. What will you do?
It was an RPG. The shot came your way.
It was an RPG. You prevented an attack.
It was a farmer with a shovel. Investigation.
Iraq. A one-way attack drone buzzes over your base at night. What will you do?
Shrapnel finds you on the way.
Your shotgun knocks it out of the sky.
killed in a drone strike in Iraq
It hits right next to you.
Mortars hit your firebase in {country}. The partner force barracks is burning. What will you do?
You drag gear and people out. Partners call you brother now.
Smoke inhalation lands you in the clinic.
You fix the point of origin and call it in. The mortars stop.
Tribal feast in {country}. The sheikh offers you the honor of eating the sheep's eye. Everyone watches. What will you do?
It's... chewy. The sheikh cheers. Your relationship is golden.
The captain eats it, glaring at you.
You realize the interpreter is softening your words to the elders, maybe on purpose. What will you do?
Your language skills hold up. Elders appreciate the effort.
Your team sergeant suggests you put in a packet for 180A, Special Forces Warrant Officer. What will you do?
Selected. Chief has a nice ring to it.
You like being on the team. Nobody can fault that.
Your team is about to be overrun. You can call a strike within 50 meters of your own position. What will you do?
The bombs land true. Everyone lives. Silver Star.
You hold with rifles and grenades.
killed when the position was overrun
Every other man on your team in the compound is down or wounded. Fighters are coming over the wall. What will you do?
You hold the breach until QRF arrives. Every wounded teammate lives. Medal of Honor.
You evacuate four men under fire. Distinguished Service Cross.
You go down carrying the fourth.
You make Master Sergeant and become the 18Z team sergeant. Your first decision: who goes to sniper school. What will you do?
Smart pick. He's an honor graduate.
Jungle training in Colombia. {buddy} gets bitten by a pit viper. Antivenom is 3 hours away by boat. What will you do?
Doc screams at you. That hasn't been taught since the 70s.
Writing evaluations for your guys. One is a good soldier but lazy. What will you do?
Honest NCOERs keep the regiment strong.
He'll get promoted anyway. You hate the system.
Your first day as ODA commander. The team sergeant has 18 years in and you have 6. What will you do?
You ask him to brief you. Trust starts here.
The team quietly freezes you out.
Your CONOP for a raid in {country} has been sitting in the approval chain for 9 days. The target is moving. What will you do?
You annoyed a major. Still not approved.
You get the target and somehow don't get fired.
Too late. The target slips away.
You brief the group commander on your plan. He asks a question you didn't anticipate. What will you do?
'Great question, sir. I'll get back to you.' He respects that.
Sounded legit. You check later and it was close enough.
He knows you're lying. He always knows.
Afghanistan. Village elders want a school built before they'll share intel on insurgents. What will you do?
The elders nod politely and tell you nothing.
A local warlord fighting your enemy wants machine guns. He's also known for brutality. What will you do?
He works with someone else. You sleep fine.
He crushes the insurgents. You don't ask how.
Human rights groups document what he did with your guns.
A drone feed shows a high-value target in a compound. Two children are playing in the courtyard. What will you do?
The target leaves. The kids are fine. You'll get another chance.
Target killed. So are others. You think about it every day.
Your team sees armed men approaching a partner checkpoint. They haven't fired. ROE says hostile intent is required. What will you do?
They're a local militia going home. Crisis averted.
They were insurgents. You were right.
violation of the rules of engagement
You control $100k of emergency project funds in {country}. A local contractor offers a 10% kickback. What will you do?
You're appointed to investigate an allegation that a team member assaulted a contractor. He's a legend in the unit. What will you do?
The facts are the facts. Justice done.
The IG finds out. Now you're under investigation.
Your partner commander wants to execute a captured ISIS fighter. 'He killed my brother.' What will you do?
The prisoner goes to a detention facility.
He does it anyway when you leave.
You hear the shot from the truck.
An aid worker is being held in a village in {country}. You have one window to hit it at night. What will you do?
Hostage rescued. All your men home. Bronze Star.
The hostage is moved. The window closes.
Some quiet civilians with good beards want to borrow your team for 'a thing.' No paperwork. What will you do?
They roll their eyes but send a memo.
Fascinating night. You can never talk about it.
Nobody told your colonel. He's livid.
In {country}, the ambassador wants your team to stay far from the border region. Your intel says that's where you're needed. What will you do?
The ambassador approves a limited presence.
Q Course officer phase. Your plan has a hole the instructor is about to find. What will you do?
Your best paid informant names a rival as an insurgent leader. The rival owns land your informant wants. What will you do?
The rival is just a farmer. You fire the informant.
You raided an innocent family's home.
A journalist wants to embed with your team in {country}. Public affairs approves. Your team sergeant hates it. What will you do?
Fair article. Your team looks professional.
The PAO complains to your colonel.
Your team's mortars got shipped to the wrong country. Mission is in 72 hours. What will you do?
A Ranger S4 owes you one. Mortars delivered.
Sandstorm rolls in. Your team is carrying a wounded partner. The helicopter says they can't land. What will you do?
You walk 8 km through the storm. He lives.
Storm passes. Bird lands. Close one.
He doesn't make it through the night.
You're selected for Command and General Staff College. Year of PowerPoint, golf, and essays. What will you do?
Staying on teams. Your career prospects narrow.
Your kid's birthday party is on a video call. You're in {country} and the connection keeps dropping. What will you do?
Your kid laughs at the frozen frame of your face. Good memory.
A captured fighter may know about a planned attack. {buddy} suggests 'stress techniques.' What will you do?
Rapport works. He gives you the plan.
He doesn't talk. Attack happens elsewhere.
He talks. You're never the same.
A partner nation general wants your team to train his personal guard, not the frontline troops. What will you do?
His guards are good now. The front still collapses.
As a major commanding an SF company, you have six ODAs and too many missions. What will you do?
You say no to the bad missions. Teams love you.
Teams are exhausted. Divorce rates spike.
Village Stability Operations. You live in the village with your team. Insurgents threaten the local police chief. What will you do?
The attack comes. You repel it. Village trusts you.
He's safe. The village thinks you abandoned it.
Your vehicle convoy must cross a pass known for ambushes. Higher wants you on the road today. What will you do?
killed in an ambush on a mountain pass
End of deployment. You write awards for your team. Higher says 'no Bronze Stars for support guys.' What will you do?
Every man gets what he earned.
Your commo sergeant gets a certificate.
Your rater says you're the second-best captain in the battalion. Only one can be 'Most Qualified.' What will you do?
As group commander, you must cut 15% of the budget. Options: training, language school, or dive teams. What will you do?
Teams start deploying without speaking the language. Ouch.
Congress wants answers on why soldiers died in a remote African ambush. You're called to testify. What will you do?
The families get answers. Some careers end. Not yours.
A general wants your partner force training numbers inflated for a briefing to Congress. What will you do?
He gets someone else to do it. Your next job is in a basement.
A major TV network wants to interview you about Green Beret operations. PAO is nervous. What will you do?
One quote goes viral. Wrong way.
A mother whose son died on your watch asks you directly: 'Was it worth it?' What will you do?
You tell her what he did and why. She holds your hand.
She sees through it. You see through it.
A partner country's defense minister gifts you a solid gold watch. The ethics rules are very clear. What will you do?
It goes to the government archives. You feel lighter.
Your group has lost three soldiers to suicide this year. What will you do?
Embedded psychologists in each battalion. The stigma starts to crack.
The Pentagon wants more Green Berets. They suggest easing SFAS standards. What will you do?
A video of brutal hazing in one of your battalions goes viral. What will you do?
It gets worse. You're relieved of command.
Washington orders a withdrawal that leaves your Syrian partners exposed. What will you do?
You write a stinging memo. You follow orders.
You're offered a cushy Pentagon job or another tour in command. What will you do?
Your star chances rise. Your soul shrinks.
You love it. Promotion odds drop.
You wake up in {country} with something long and cold moving in your sleeping bag. What will you do?
It leaves. You don't sleep again for a week.
You fly out of the bag and the team laughs for days.
It bites on the way out.
A scrappy stray dog adopts your team in {country}. Regulations say no pets. What will you do?
The dog barks at insurgents and becomes a legend.
You pay to ship it to the States. It's now living its best life.
A care package from a school in Ohio arrives with crayon drawings and 40 lbs of beef jerky. What will you do?
You hear a pop in your shoulder going for a deadlift PR in front of the team. What will you do?
Six weeks of bands and ice. Back to full strength.
It heals on its own. Lucky.
A hurricane is bearing down on Fort Bragg. Your unit is tasked to help evacuate the local area. What will you do?
You carry grandmas out of flooded houses.
A villager you helped years ago tracks you down on social media to say thanks. Her daughter is a doctor now. What will you do?
You stare at the message for a long time. This is why.
The last MRE in the box. It's Veggie Omelet. {buddy} is hungrily eyeing it. What will you do?
{buddy} eats it, gags, and thanks you. True friendship.
Pararescue Indoctrination Course. The instructors make you do underwater laps with no breaks. Your vision is going dark at the edges. What do you do?
You touch the wall and gasp. Instructor nods.
You black out. Instructors drag you up. Shallow water blackout scare.
Safe, but it's a fail. You'll have to redo it.
Efficient and calm. You make it.
Buddy breathing drill: you and {buddy} share one snorkel while instructors harass you. He's hogging the air. What do you do?
He gets the rhythm. You both pass.
You both panic and surface. Fail.
You get air. Instructor wasn't looking.
It's week three of Indoc. Half the class is gone. You're freezing, sore and nobody would blame you for quitting. What do you do?
You stop thinking about the end and focus on the next meal.
You quit. The regret lasts years.
That Others May Live. You hold onto it.
Fins swim in choppy water. A cramp seizes your calf halfway through. What do you do?
It loosens up. You finish on time.
Safety boat picks you up. You'll retest.
Combat Diver Course in Panama City. Your rebreather is acting up during a night dive. What do you do?
Oxygen toxicity seizure. Your buddy saves you.
At military freefall school, your body position is unstable and you keep spinning. Your instructor is next to you in the air. What do you do?
You pull while unstable. Line twists. Hard landing.
He signals legs out. It works.
The paramedic phase is brutal. Pharmacology exams, clinical rotations, and you're sleeping four hours a night. How do you keep up?
You pass. Your study group becomes family.
The group is more social than studious.
You fail the cardiology exam. Retest.
During a civilian ER rotation, a gunshot victim comes in. The nurse tells you to get an IV in now. Your hands are shaking. What do you do?
You blow the vein. She does it herself.
Wrong site. The doctor takes over.
You graduate from the Pararescue Apprentice Course. An old PJ hands you the maroon beret. How do you mark the day?
You read the names of the fallen. You understand the beret now.
A long night of stories and laughter.
Your dad can't stop saying 'my son the PJ'.
You're on alert in {country}. The radio goes off: 'Pedro, Pedro, Pedro.' A helicopter is down. What's your first move?
Glad you did. You'll need everything.
The team waits on you. Not great.
Your Pave Hawk lands under fire to pick up a wounded soldier. Rounds are snapping overhead. He's 50 meters away. What do you do?
You drag him back to the bird. Wheels up.
Gunners silence the enemy. Then you go.
A soldier's leg is nearly severed by an IED. Your first tourniquet isn't stopping the bleeding. What do you do?
He bleeds out in the helicopter.
Despite everything you did, a young Marine dies in your helicopter. You can't stop thinking about it. What do you do?
He tells you about his first loss. It helps.
His mother writes back. She thanks you for being there.
Hoist training over trees. The rotor wash is spinning you on the cable. What do you do?
You slam into a tree trunk.
{buddy} wants to fill the team leader's truck with packing peanuts. It would be legendary. Are you in?
He laughs for days and swears revenge.
Night jump into the ocean with a zodiac boat. You land tangled in your canopy lines. Waves are breaking over you. What do you do?
You free yourself and reach the boat.
You swallow a lot of seawater.
A hiker is stranded on a ledge in a training area. Your team leader asks you to rappel down to him. Wind is picking up. What do you do?
Rescue successful. The hiker hugs you.
A gust slams you into the cliff.
The wind dies down. Safe rescue an hour later.
Your med bag is missing a chest seal before a mission. Supply is closed. What do you do?
An improvised chest seal works fine in the field.
There's a party in the barracks. Someone brought something a lot stronger than beer. A random drug test is likely next week. What do you do?
Three people pop on the test. You don't.
Your annual PJ fitness test includes a 25-meter underwater swim and pull-ups. You've been slacking. What do you do?
In the altitude chamber, the instructor has you remove your mask to see hypoxia symptoms. You feel giddy. What do you do?
Searching for a downed pilot's beacon in a forest. Your signal is weak and bouncing. What do you do?
You fall out of the tree.
Too slow. Another team finds him first.
After a disaster rescue, you find a scared dog in the rubble. Your team leader says no animals on the aircraft. What do you do?
A family adopts it. You see a photo later.
The crew adopts it as a mascot.
A soldier pulled from an icy river is barely breathing. He's cold to the touch. What do you do?
He stabilizes. 'Not dead until warm and dead.'
His heart goes into a bad rhythm.
Driving home, you come across a bad car crash. No ambulance yet. You have your personal med kit. What do you do?
You stabilize the driver. The news calls you a hero.
The driver doesn't make it. You did everything right.
You roll your ankle during a training jump. A long-awaited course starts next week. What do you do?
You miss the course but heal properly.
It breaks on the first day.
During a trauma lane exercise, two moulaged patients scream for help at once. One is bleeding, one isn't breathing. Who first?
Too slow on the second patient.
During a training swim, {buddy} gets stung by a jellyfish and starts panicking. What do you do?
He's fine. Owes you a beer.
He kicks you in the face.
At SERE school, you're hungry for days. You find a lizard. Do you eat it?
The team decides to give you a nickname after you fell out of the helicopter cabin in training. They pick 'Gravity'. How do you react?
An F-16 pilot ejected over hostile territory in {country}. His beacon is active but enemy trucks are moving toward him. What's the plan?
You reach him first. He cries when he sees you.
The trucks arrive at the same time.
A-10s clear the area. Clean pickup.
The enemy reaches him first. He's captured.
Enemy chases the decoy. You get the pilot.
They split up. You fight your way in.
A rocket hits a base dining hall. 20 wounded, three PJs. You're the senior medic on scene. How do you triage?
Some patients deteriorate faster than expected.
Two patients: a US soldier with minor wounds and an enemy fighter who's critical. Your team leader says treat the American. What do you do?
The fighter dies. You think about it for years.
A helicopter crashed at 11,000 feet in {country}. The air is thin and snow is coming. Survivors may be inside. What do you do?
You find two survivors. Both make it.
Safer, but nobody survives the night.
A daring hoist through a cloud gap. Survivors out.
The bird loses power at altitude.
A cargo ship crewman went overboard 600 miles out. You'll jump from an HC-130 at night into 15-foot seas. Do you lead the jump?
You find him alive after four hours.
Hard landing in the swells. You still find him.
You're on standby for a crewed capsule splashdown. If something goes wrong, PJs jump in. The capsule hits rough water. What do you do?
You stabilize the capsule. Astronauts safe.
Swells slam you into the capsule.
Your patient's blood type tag says O-negative but the bracelet says A-positive. You have only O-negative blood. What do you do?
You keep seeing the faces of the patients you couldn't save. You haven't slept properly in weeks. What do you do?
It's not weakness. It saved you.
He gets it. You start to heal.
Hurricane floods. Families stranded on rooftops. Your Pave Hawk has fuel for four more hoists. Five roofs. Who do you leave?
Another crew reaches the last roof. Everyone lives.
You save everyone and land on fumes.
Emergency landing in a parking lot. Not great.
A patient has a tension pneumothorax. The needle decompression didn't hold. The bumpy ride makes it worse. What do you do?
Air rushes out. He breathes again.
You're promoted to team leader. A young PJ keeps freezing during live missions. What do you do?
He becomes one of your best PJs.
Safer for the team. He's crushed.
The hoist cable jams with you and a patient 40 feet below the helicopter. The pilot can't hold hover much longer. What do you do?
They lower you to the ground. Plan B works.
The ground is rougher than expected.
A downed pilot is hiding in a ravine. Enemies are searching nearby. His radio is breaking up. What do you tell him?
He stays still. You find him first.
A team member fell 30 feet into a cave. He's conscious but has a spinal injury. Extraction will take hours. What do you do?
An earthquake in {country}. A child is trapped under concrete and the building is unstable. Engineers say no. What do you do?
You pull her out minutes before the building collapses.
Nobody goes in. You hear her crying for hours.
A helicopter ditched in the ocean. The crew is trapped inside at 30 feet. Visibility is near zero. What do you do?
You pull two crew members out alive.
Divers arrive. It's a recovery now.
After 16 years, your body is breaking down. Your family wants you to retire at 20. Your team wants you for one more deployment. What do you do?
Your experience saves lives. Your knees hate you.
Your Humvee ambulance rolls on a mountain road. You and the patient are thrown around. What do you do?
You shield him. He's fine. You're bruised.
You're fine. The patient is worse.
The pilot says the weather is too bad to fly. A soldier will die without evacuation. What do you do?
The pilot agrees. You make it.
He refuses. You're angry for weeks.
You keep the soldier alive all night. He makes it.
A soldier has burns on 60% of his body. He's screaming. You have limited morphine. What do you do?
He calms. You focus on fluids.
His airway was swelling. You saved him.
A news crew filmed your team hoisting a stranded hiker off a cliff. They want an on-camera interview with the 'hero'. What do you say?
You name the pilots and the flight engineer. Classy.
Quiet professional. The clip goes viral anyway.
The team prints your quote and tapes it to your locker.
You're in open ocean holding a survivor, waiting 20 minutes for the helicopter. A large shark starts circling. What do you do?
It loses interest. Worst 20 minutes of your life.
It bumps, then bites your fin and leg.
Face it and jab its nose
It veers off and doesn't come back.
{buddy} wants you both to get the PJ guardian angel tattoo after this deployment. Your spouse hates tattoos. Do you get it?
Matching angels. Your spouse rolls their eyes and secretly likes it.
He gets it alone and shows it off for a month.
A private medical contractor offers you triple your pay to work as an overseas medic. You're two years from a pension. What do you do?
The money is great. You miss the team within a month.
Two more years. The team is glad you stayed.
Your spouse says your kids barely know you. You were away 200 days last year between deployments and schools. What do you do?
Your kids start running to the door when you get home.
Your career soars. The house feels colder.
Two weeks, no phone. It helps a lot.
You get recalled on day three.
A soldier collapses on a 120-degree patrol in {country}. He's confused and hot to the touch. Ice is limited. What do you do?
His temperature drops fast. He walks out of the hospital.
He seizes before you can cool him.
You're a freefall instructor. Your student's main chute streamers below you and he's not cutting away. What do you do?
You reach him and signal cutaway. Reserve opens. He lives.
You collide with him. Both reserves open, both of you hurt.
He hears you and cuts away. Reserve opens.
His automatic device fires late. He survives, badly hurt.
A mass casualty exercise has 100 screaming role players. Your team is overwhelmed and evaluators are watching. What do you do?
Evaluators note it. Knowing your limits is the point.
Your Pave Hawk clips a power line during a night approach. Alarms scream and the aircraft lurches. What do you do?
The pilots wrestle it down. Hard landing. Everyone lives.
You strap him down just in time. He's unhurt.
A PJ you served with for 10 years was killed on a rescue. His widow asks you to speak at the funeral. What do you say?
The church laughs and cries at the same time. She hugs you.
Dignified. You can't trust your voice for more.
You're asked to inventory a fallen teammate's belongings before they're sent home. You find things his wife shouldn't see. What do you do?
His family remembers him the way he'd want.
By the book. It causes his family pain.
A snowmobiler fell through a frozen lake near your base in Alaska. Local rescuers are 40 minutes out. Your team is 5 minutes away. What do you do?
You crawl across the ice and pull him out alive.
The ice breaks under you too. Your team hauls you both out.
He grabs it with frozen hands. Out.
His hands can't grip. Too cold.
A sailor on a fishing ship 800 miles at sea has a burst appendix. You'd parachute in from an HC-130 and treat him for two days. Do you jump?
You land next to the ship and keep him alive until port.
Rough water landing. He still lives, thanks to your partner.
They nail it. Good to see.
Night before your first combat rescue alert shift. {buddy} can't sleep and keeps asking 'what if'. What do you do?
You both admit you're scared. You both sleep.
At a crowded beach on leave, a lifeguard is struggling with an unconscious swimmer. You're a trained paramedic. What do you do?
He coughs up water and breathes. The crowd claps.
Paramedics take over. You did everything you could.
You watch from the sand. It bothers you.
An instructor in the Apprentice Course says your casualty care is sloppy and you'll get someone killed. It stings. How do you respond?
He spends an extra hour with you. You get better.
He makes you redo the lane five times.
You're at Combat Rescue Officer selection. After a 20-hour day, the board asks why you didn't just become a pilot. What do you say?
You talk about the pilots who came home because of PJs. Selected.
It sounds rehearsed. Not selected this year.
The old CRO on the board laughs out loud. Selected.
The pilot on the board does not laugh.
Admit you failed the eye exam
They wonder if this is your second choice.
You must plan a rescue for a downed crew 200 miles inside {country}. You have one HC-130 for fuel and two Pave Hawks. What's the plan?
In, refuel, pick up, out. The crew is home by breakfast.
The enemy guessed the obvious route. You divert.
Air defenses chase ghosts while you grab the crew.
Timing collapses. The tanker is in the wrong place.
Weather is marginal and the downed pilot's radio battery is dying. {co} asks you for a go or no-go recommendation right now. What do you say?
You thread the weather and find him with minutes of battery left.
Icing forces an abort halfway there.
The weather clears and he's still hiding. Clean pickup.
By dawn, his radio is silent.
The 'pilot' on the radio isn't using his authentication words correctly. It could be stress, or it could be a trap. What do you do?
It was just a rattled pilot. You bring him home.
Muzzle flashes erupt as you land. It was a trap.
He knows his dog's name. Verified. Clean pickup.
The delay lets a patrol close in. He's captured.
Drone shows him alone. Safe rescue.
The drone is late. Hours lost.
One slot left on a dangerous rescue. A veteran PJ with two kids, or an eager new guy who's never been tested. Who do you pick?
Calm hands, clean mission. Experience matters.
He's brilliant under pressure. A star is born.
He hesitates at a key moment. Everyone's fine, barely.
You're offered a Pentagon staff job. Great for your career, but you'd leave your squadron right before a deployment. What do you do?
You learn the budget game. Your old team sends memes about your desk.
Your PJs notice. You'll go next cycle.
During your mission brief, a junior PJ raises his hand and points out a real flaw in your fuel plan. Everyone is watching you. What do you do?
The team trusts you more. And you don't run out of gas.
The Pave Hawk lands with fuel warnings blaring. He was right.
You're running a joint rescue cell with allied forces. Their commander wants to lead the next recovery. What do you do?
They do great. The alliance is stronger.
Language confusion slows the launch by an hour.
They feel sidelined and stop sharing intel.
They handle security, you handle medicine. Perfect.
Two bosses, one radio net. Messy.
Your promotion board meets next month. Your record is good, not great. Your mentor says one more deployment would help. What do you do?
A pilot your team rescued wants to thank you on a national morning show. Public affairs is thrilled. What do you do?
You name every PJ on air. Recruiting numbers spike.
Your team gets the spotlight they earned.
Public affairs is disappointed. Quiet professionals, though.
Your squadron's training budget gets slashed. You can fund combat dive or military freefall requalification, not both. What stays?
Maritime rescue stays sharp. Freefall currency lapses.
Deep-insertion stays ready. The divers grumble.
You find leftover year-end money. Both funded.
Higher tells you to stop asking.
A PJ dies during a water training exercise you planned. The safety investigation starts tomorrow. How do you handle it?
Investigators find an equipment failure. You still lose sleep.
The board sees you as defensive. Career damage.
As a CRO, you can fly on tonight's dangerous rescue or run it from the ops center with better comms. Where do you go?
Your PJs see you on the hoist. Respect earned.
A round punches through the cabin and into your leg.
You coordinate fighters, tankers and the helos perfectly.
An allied pilot is down in contested territory. Your tasking says US personnel only, but you're closest. What do you do?
Approved in eight minutes. He's rescued.
Denied. Another nation's team arrives too late.
He's rescued. His government sends a thank-you letter.
Rescue works. You're relieved for disobeying.
After a deployment with heavy losses, your squadron's morale is in the basement. Two PJs have put in separation papers. What do you do?
Barbecue, kids, and a bounce house. It helps more than you'd think.
Embedded mental health makes a real difference.
Nobody wants to be seen going.
Two more separation papers land on your desk.
Your Pave Hawk takes fire on final approach to the survivor. The pilot looks at you. You're the mission commander. What's the call?
Gunships clear the area. You go back in and get him.
The survivor is moved by the enemy before you return.
Thirty seconds on the ground. Survivor aboard. Gone.
Rounds rake the cabin. Two crew wounded, you among them.
A PJ under your command gave the wrong drug dose during a rescue. The patient survived. He comes to you, terrified. What do you do?
A no-fault review fixes a confusing drug kit layout.
The hospital flags it. Now it's a cover-up.
You're offered a two-year exchange tour with a British rescue unit. Your spouse would have to move overseas. What do you do?
You learn their mountain tactics. And how to queue properly.
Your spouse is relieved. Another officer goes.
A typhoon flattened coastal towns in an allied nation. You're leading the US rescue element. Where do you focus first?
Your teams pull 40 people from collapsed homes in two days.
Your PJs relieve exhausted local medics.
You reach villages no one else could. Hundreds helped.
Your father has days to live. A critical recovery mission launches in 48 hours and you're the only CRO qualified. What do you do?
You hold his hand at the end. Your deputy runs the mission fine.
The mission succeeds. You miss the funeral. It haunts you.
You're teaching survival skills to a group of fighter pilots. One senior pilot says it's beneath him and refuses to participate. What do you do?
You tell him about a pilot who lived because of this class. He's first in line.
He's ordered to participate. He sulks all week.
After a successful rescue, a PJ admits he skipped a required safety step to reach the patient faster. It worked. What do you do?
He learns judgment matters. Others may cut corners now, though.
He's annoyed, but the standard holds.
You push the change up. It's adopted Air Force-wide.
The bureaucracy stalls it for a year.
One of your PJs did something truly heroic under fire. {co} wants to downgrade the award to save paperwork. What do you do?
He receives the higher award. Deserved.
The PJ gets the lesser award. He notices.
A new rescue hoist failed twice in testing. Program managers want you to sign off on fielding it. What's your recommendation?
The flaw is fixed first. Nobody falls.
It works fine in the field.
It fails during a real rescue. People get hurt.
Rockets hit your base and fighters breach the perimeter. Your PJs are medics, but they're also trained shooters. How do you employ them?
Your PJs run a casualty collection point. Nobody who reaches them dies.
Your team helps throw back the attack.
You're hit by shrapnel on the wall.
As {rank}, you command a rescue group. Budget planners want to cut a Pave Hawk squadron. You're asked to testify. What's your angle?
He tells his story. The room goes silent. Funding saved.
Moving testimony. The cut happens anyway.
Your numbers on lives saved per dollar win the day.
Future wars may not have air superiority. Slow helicopters may not survive. How do you reshape rescue doctrine?
Your 'survive and wait' concept becomes doctrine.
After 28 years, your body is a collection of old injuries. You could retire, or take one last command tour. What do you do?
Your retirement ceremony is packed with people you rescued.
Your knees file a formal complaint.
You're dedicating a new memorial to pararescuemen killed in action. Families are in the front row. What do you say?
You tell how one of them died saving a stranger. Everyone feels it.
A rescue under your command failed, and the pilot died. A news outlet is running the story tomorrow. How do you respond?
You explain what went wrong. The family respects it.
Speculation fills the void. It gets worse.
A new lieutenant asks you for the single most important thing about leading PJs. What do you tell her?
She writes it down. Years later, she's a great commander.
She becomes famous for brutal, realistic training.
At a NATO rescue conference, allies propose shared rescue procedures. Some of your staff worry about security. What do you do?
Allied crews can now rescue each other seamlessly.
A respected senior chief in your group is accused of harassing a junior airman. He's a legend. What do you do?
Facts come out. Justice is done either way.
It doesn't go away. Now it's about you too.
Half your group's helicopters are grounded for parts. Readiness reports look terrible. What do you do?
A retired PJ you once led calls at 2 AM. He's drinking and talking about the patients he lost. What do you do?
You sit with him until sunrise. He gets help that week.
He says thanks. You worry for weeks.
At Thanksgiving, your aunt asks if you're a pilot. You try to explain pararescue for the fifth year in a row. What do you say?
She nods. She still thinks you're a pilot.
At a school career day, a kid asks what a PJ actually does. What do you tell him?
He says he wants to do it too.
The whole class loses its mind.
There's an open-water memorial swim for fallen PJs this weekend. It's cold and three miles. Will you join?
A guy at the base pool challenges you to a 400-meter race. He looks suspiciously fit. Do you accept?
You win by a body length.
He swam in college. You lose badly.
The team watches a rescue movie where the hero does CPR on a conscious man. {buddy} is losing his mind. Do you join?
It's fun if you turn off your brain.
Assessment and Selection starts with a ruck run in the North Carolina heat. Half the class looks like they already regret it. How do you start?
You finish near the front. A cadre member writes something down.
You blow up at mile six and limp in at the back.
You finish strong and unremarkable. In A&S, that's a win.
Cadre notice you carrying someone else's water. Team players get remembered.
You both come in late. Nobody remembers why.
The cadre won't say how far today's ruck is. It's been four hours. Rumor says it never ends. What's your mindset?
You stop counting and keep moving. Turns out it was 18 miles.
Your feet bleed through your socks but you finish. Barely.
He actually tells you. You're stunned.
'As far as it takes, candidate.' He writes your number down.
You think about it hard, then don't. The doubt costs you, though.
A psychologist asks why you want to be a Raider and how you handle failure. Your answer could decide your career. What do you say?
You talk about your failures plainly. The psych nods. Good sign.
You ramble. The psych's face gives nothing away.
'So you want to be in a movie?' Not great.
You say Raiders are a team sport. The board loves it.
It sounds rehearsed because it is.
Your A&S team must carry a waterlogged log and sandbags across a swamp. Your teammate {buddy} keeps letting go. How do you handle it?
Cadre see you take more weight without complaining.
Your back tweaks under the extra load.
He grips tighter. It works, but he hates you.
The cadre mark you as a poor teammate.
You organize a rotation. Leadership noticed.
The rotation falls apart in the mud.
Your name is read at the end of A&S. You're going to the Individual Training Course. A cadre shakes your hand. How do you celebrate?
Your mom cries. Your dad pretends he isn't.
You eat three burgers and a whole pizza. No regrets.
You wake up still in your boots.
Shoot house day at ITC. You're number two through the door, and the room has hostages and targets mixed together. What's your approach?
Clean hits, zero hostages tagged. Instructor grunts approval.
You put two rounds into a hostage target. Long debrief.
Slower, but perfect. That's what they want.
Too slow. The number one man is clearing your corner.
You both end up looking at the same corner.
You're 'captured' during SERE training. The interrogator is very convincing and you haven't slept in a day. How do you hold up?
You give nothing beyond what's allowed. You'll never forget this week.
You say something you shouldn't have. Instructors note it.
He does not find you funny. More stress positions.
Silence made them work harder on you.
ITC assigns you a language for foreign internal defense work. Classes run late after long days. How hard do you study?
You can order food and ask for a village elder. Progress.
You're exhausted and still mixing up verbs.
You pass. Barely. Interpreters will love you.
A local shop owner becomes your tutor. Huge improvement.
He mostly teaches you slang and insults.
An old instructor tells you about the 1942 Makin Island raid, launched from submarines. He asks what 'Spiritus Invictus' means to you. Your answer?
He stares at you until you feel very small.
ITC graduation. You're now a Critical Skills Operator. {buddy} pins you and grins. What do you do afterward?
Your team raises a glass in silence. It hits harder than you expected.
Great night, nothing broken, nobody arrested.
A bar fight on graduation night. Your commander is not impressed.
Your hometown treats you like a celebrity for a weekend.
You're the new guy on your team in {unit}. Someone has to clean the team room, inventory gear, and make coffee. Guess who. Your attitude?
Senior guys notice. The coffee is also good.
Everyone saw it. Including the team chief.
You turn inventory into a game. Even the old guys join.
Nobody plays. You still do it alone.
You're slotted for combat diver training. Pool comp is legendary: instructors rip off your regulator underwater. How do you face it?
You panic and bolt for the surface. Fail.
Weeks of breath holds pay off. Smooth pass.
You get a later slot. Someone else takes yours.
On a static line jump, your canopy twists and you're spinning. The ground is coming fast. What do you do?
The twists unwind. You land with a story.
You land hard and wreck your ankle.
Reserve opens. Rough landing, but you walk away.
Both canopies tangle. You hit hard.
The canopy fixes itself. Pure luck.
You hit the ground like a sack of bricks.
After a 3,000-round day, someone has to police brass in the rain. {buddy} suggests hiding a few bags behind the berm. What do you do?
Nobody checks. You go home early.
Range control finds it. Everyone gets smoked, then you get NJP.
He rolls his eyes, but helps.
Your Marine Special Operations Team deploys to {country} to train local forces. On the plane, {buddy} asks if you're nervous. Your answer?
He admits he is too. You both feel better.
You're teaching marksmanship to partner soldiers in {country}. One keeps sweeping the line with his muzzle. How do you correct him?
He gets it. Nobody dies today.
He nods and keeps doing it.
He's humiliated in front of his unit. Rapport drops.
Letting their leaders lead is the whole point of FID.
His sergeant shrugs. It's a long day.
A village elder in {country} invites you for tea. It's your third cup and your stomach is not okay. Refusing could be rude. What do you do?
Strong rapport. He shares useful information.
You spend two days hugging a latrine.
He's offended. The meeting ends early.
Your patrol takes fire from a tree line in {country}. Partner forces scatter. {buddy} is pinned behind a low wall. What do you do?
{buddy} sprints to cover. The enemy breaks contact.
A round finds you as you rise up to shoot.
You get them firing back. The ambush collapses.
You get hit running between positions.
Mortars land on the tree line. Contact over.
Support is 30 minutes out. It's a long 30 minutes.
Your NVG battery dies halfway through a night movement. It's pitch black and silence is critical. What now?
You practiced this blindfolded. It pays off.
You drop the spare. It's gone forever.
You follow by touch. Embarrassing but effective.
Nobody saw it. You got lucky.
The whole team hisses at you. Never again.
On a foot patrol, you spot disturbed dirt and a wire near the path. The team is 20 meters behind you. What do you do?
EOD confirms an IED. You may have saved lives.
It's a buried cable. Better safe than sorry.
The detour had a second device.
Your team chief runs a PT session that leaves everyone puking. {buddy} says you should complain to the officer. What do you do?
Next week, you're the one not puking.
The officer laughs and tells the chief. The next PT is worse.
Ask the chief to program it
He's impressed you care. You help plan PT now.
On a stopover in Okinawa, {buddy} wants to hit Gate 2 Street after curfew. The liberty rules are strict. Do you go?
You hear the next morning that a bunch of guys got caught.
Shore patrol catches you after curfew. NJP.
You get back in time. Responsible fun.
The taxi gets lost. You're 10 minutes late.
You want to post a photo of your kit and team on social media. It looks very cool. What do you do?
The team's faces are visible. OPSEC brief, in person, loudly.
Gets a ton of likes and no trouble.
The geotag showed your base. Oops.
Smart. The best operators are boring online.
One slot is open for a sniper course. You and {buddy} both want it. The team chief asks you to make your case. What do you do?
Your numbers win. You get the slot.
He never forgets it. Next slot is yours.
You get it. He knows what you did.
The chief sees right through it.
During a sniper stalk, an instructor walks within three feet of your ghillie suit. Your nose itches terribly. What do you do?
He walks past. You take your shot. Pass.
He spots the barrel glint anyway.
Somehow, you get away with it.
'Got you.' The instructor taps your head.
You tear something in your shoulder during fast-rope training. Reporting it could cost you a deployment. What do you do?
Surgery and rehab. You'll be back.
It heals on its own. You dodged a bullet.
It fully tears on deployment. Now it's surgery and a long rehab.
He sets you up with a physical therapy plan.
He reports it anyway. Medical hold.
Fast-roping from a hovering helicopter at night, your gloves start smoking. The ground's about 20 feet down. What do you do?
Your palms sting but you land fine.
You burn through and drop the last 10 feet.
Surprise room inspection. Your roommate {buddy} has energy drinks and protein powder all over the floor. What's your move?
You pass with seconds to spare. He owes you.
He gets yelled at. You're fine.
{buddy} says you can sell spare issued gear online for good money. 'Nobody counts it,' he says. What do you do?
Two months later, he's under investigation.
Easy money. Your stomach still turns.
NCIS finds the listings. Career over.
{buddy} wants to get matching Raider skull tattoos the night after graduation. Do you join?
It looks great. Your mom does not agree.
Small and classy. You'll thank yourself at 50.
He calls you boring for a week.
During a land nav event in the desert, your GPS dies and the terrain all looks the same. Water is running low. What do you do?
Old school skills win. You hit every point.
You walk five miles in the wrong direction.
You spot a landmark and reorient.
You fail the event, but you're alive.
During water confidence training, you have to tread water in full kit for 10 minutes. Your arms burn. What do you do?
You drop what you're allowed to. Smart.
You dropped the rifle. Not allowed.
As {rank} you've been asked to take over as team chief. It means more paperwork and less trigger time. Do you accept?
Your team trusts you. You lose sleep and gain gray hairs.
You keep shooting, but the command remembers.
Your CO agrees to keep you in the field.
Partner force NCOs in {country} defer every decision to their officers. You want them leading. How do you build that?
A partner sergeant runs a perfect patrol. Huge win.
Their officers feel undermined and shut it down.
Slow but lasting. The officers buy in.
Things work while you're there. Not after.
You discover the partner force commander in {country} is selling fuel you provided on the black market. What's your move?
Your command addresses it diplomatically. He's replaced.
Nothing happens. He knows you reported him.
He freezes your team out of all operations.
The mission continues. Your conscience doesn't sleep well.
Night raid on a compound in {country}. The breach charge fails to fire. Dogs are barking. Your team is stacked at the door. What now?
The door gives on the third hit. Target captured.
Someone inside fires through the door.
Window entry catches them totally off guard.
The target escapes out the back.
The delay gives them time to prepare.
You're watching a man you think is your high-value target. Facial match is 70%. The window closes in minutes. Your call?
He turns. Confirmed match. Clean capture.
It's him. The team takes him without a shot.
Wrong man. A very awkward release and apology.
Your commander makes the call and owns it.
You've been in a hide site watching a smuggling route for four days. A goat herder is walking straight toward your position. What do you do?
He passes within 10 feet. Never sees you.
His dog finds you. Mission compromised, exfil early.
You slip away and set up again.
Rock slide. He definitely heard that.
Safe, but you lose the observation.
Your vehicle convoy is hit by an IED followed by heavy machine gun fire. The lead vehicle is burning with men inside. What do you do?
You drag two men from the flames under fire.
Your fire silences the gun. Others pull the men free.
A round finds you behind the turret.
Jets arrive. The enemy breaks off.
Air is 20 minutes out. Too long.
Your team is overrun at an outpost. You're the senior Marine left standing. Ammunition is low. How do you fight?
Your counterattack shatters the assault. The outpost holds.
You're cut down leading the charge.
You hold until the QRF arrives.
The retreat is chaotic. Equipment is left behind.
{buddy} is badly hit. The medevac bird won't land until the LZ is secured. You have three Marines and a partner squad. What do you do?
LZ goes cold. {buddy} makes it out.
You take a round securing it.
Carry him to an alternate LZ
He doesn't make it. You carry that forever.
The pilots come in anyway. Legends.
The bird takes fire and waves off.
After a firefight, you find a civilian was killed in crossfire. The partner force wants to leave it out of the report. What do you do?
It's painful, but right. The family gets compensation.
A drone feed contradicts the report. Investigation.
Since your last deployment, fireworks make you hit the ground and you barely sleep. Your spouse is worried. What do you do?
It's hard to talk, but it helps. Sleep slowly returns.
It works for a night. Then it doesn't.
He's been through the same. You aren't alone.
He changes the subject. He's not ready either.
You've deployed three times in five years. Your spouse says they feel like a single parent. They want you to consider leaving. What do you do?
Instructor duty. Home every night. Your family breathes.
You put in the effort. Things improve.
Military OneSource helps. You both listen better.
Sessions keep getting canceled for training.
A new team commander wants to skip rehearsals before a live mission. Your team is uneasy. As senior enlisted, what do you do?
He listens. Rehearsals happen. Mission goes clean.
He overrules you. The mission gets messy.
You've made an enemy for the rest of the tour.
Your team rehearses on their own time. He comes around.
A new CSO on your team keeps struggling on the range and is losing confidence. The others are mocking him. What do you do?
Within a month he's outshooting the mockers.
He improves a little. It's a start.
The team gets the message. Morale improves.
He requests a transfer out. Wasted talent.
You're range safety officer for a demolitions range. A junior Marine sets a charge with the wrong time fuse length. What do you do?
You catch it before anyone gets hurt. Teaching moment.
The charge goes early while you work on it.
{buddy} shows up to morning formation smelling like a brewery for the third time this month. What do you do?
He enters a program. He's grateful years later.
He feels betrayed and won't talk to you.
He gets his act together. This time.
He gets a DUI. Your cover-up comes out.
By the book. He's off the team.
Your interpreter in {country} has saved your life twice. His family is getting threats. His special visa is stuck in paperwork. What do you do?
Months later, he lands in the US. He sends a photo of his kids.
The visa is still pending. You stop sleeping well.
Your chain of command is annoyed you went outside.
Accept it's out of your hands
You never hear from him again.
You're leading a combat rubber raiding craft insertion. The swells are bigger than forecast and the engine sputters. What do you do?
You hit the beach on time, soaked.
The boat flips in the surf. Gear lost.
Nobody likes it, but nobody drowns.
You miss the window by an hour.
Night HALO jump into {country}. At 25,000 feet your oxygen mask feels loose. The green light is on. What do you do?
Seal holds. Perfect canopy flight to the DZ.
Hypoxia hits in freefall. You barely pull in time.
You jump on the second pass and land miles from the team.
The swap takes too long. Jumpmaster is furious.
Your unit wants you for another rotation. You've been home seven months. Your knees are shot and your kid's in kindergarten. What do you do?
The team needs your experience. Your kid sends drawings.
Your sergeant major agrees. You coach T-ball.
You go to the schoolhouse. Home for dinner.
You catch a few senior guys making a new operator do humiliating things in the team room. They call it 'tradition'. What do you do?
Uncomfortable for a day. It never happens again.
Investigation follows. Some resentment, but it's done.
It becomes a news story months later. Your name comes up.
You're attached to a government agency team in {country}. Their rules are vague and their requests are sketchy. What do you do?
They grumble, but respect your lines.
An inspector general report lands on your desk.
Legal sorts it out. Slow but safe.
Your team's assault dog freezes at a doorway and won't go in. The handler is wounded. What do you do?
Turns out the room was rigged with explosives. Good dog.
The room was empty. Lost precious time.
MARSOC offers a large reenlistment bonus. A defense contractor offers triple your salary. What do you do?
Bonus banked. Back to the team.
Big money. You miss the brotherhood within a month.
Bonus and your choice of assignment.
You get a smaller bonus and a desk job.
After a long patrol, a junior Marine on your team realizes his rifle is missing. It's 2 AM. What do you do?
Found in the back of a truck. Crisis averted.
Not found. Investigation, and everyone loses their weekend.
Painful, but the right move. It's found next day.
You're 34 and the young guys are smoking you on the run. Your PFT is this week. How do you prepare?
You pull a calf muscle the day before.
Second class score. The young guys never let it go.
Partner soldiers you trained refuse to fight after their pay is stolen by their own officers. An operation starts tomorrow. What do you do?
You get the money released. They fight hard.
Your team does it alone. It works.
A partner soldier has been staring at your team strangely and asking where you sleep. Your gut says something is wrong. What do you do?
Counterintelligence finds he's been contacted by insurgents.
False alarm. Rapport takes a small hit.
You catch him with a phone full of enemy contacts.
Your team's small surveillance drone crashes in a market in {country}. Kids are already picking it up. What do you do?
You trade candy for the drone. Diplomacy.
A crowd forms. Tense moment, mission scrubbed.
Data's gone. Kids get a cool toy.
They 'lose' the drone. It ends up for sale.
Your old gunnery sergeant is retiring after 22 years. They ask you to give a speech. What kind of speech?
The whole room is crying laughing.
One joke goes too far. His wife isn't laughing.
The old man tears up for the first time ever.
He appreciates it. He hates speeches.
You're now an ITC instructor. A student is talented but arrogant and dangerous on the range. Do you drop him?
He gets humbled and becomes a great operator.
He has a negligent discharge. Thankfully into the dirt.
The shrapnel in your back starts acting up during a long ruck. You have miles left. What do you do?
Smart. Doc gives you meds and light duty.
You take command of a Marine Special Operations Team. Your team chief has more combat experience than you. How do you lead?
The team chief becomes your closest ally.
The team quietly decides you're a problem.
Lead from the front in PT
You crush every workout. They notice.
You injure yourself trying too hard.
Intelligence says a bomb-maker is at a house tonight. The approval chain will take 12 hours. You have the team ready now. What do you do?
By the time it's approved, he's gone. But you followed the rules.
Approved in an hour. Target captured.
Success. Nobody asks too many questions.
The US ambassador in {country} is nervous about your team's operations. She wants fewer raids. How do you respond?
She calls your commander to complain.
Fewer raids, more partner growth. Everyone's happy.
Your team gets restricted to base. Ouch.
A strike could kill a key militant leader, but there's a chance children are in the building. You have authority. What's your call?
He gets away. Later footage shows kids playing outside. You were right.
Civilians were inside. You'll carry this forever.
He moves to a vehicle. Clean strike.
As a Marine officer, you're screening for MARSOC. You'll have to compete with enlisted candidates in A&S. How do you approach it?
You're dropped. Try again next year.
A journalist embedded with partner forces wants to interview you. Public affairs is unavailable. What do you do?
Story runs and makes partner forces look great.
One quote is taken out of context. Huge headache.
He swears on the record. Many times.
Midway through a raid, you realize the building is a wedding party, not a militant safehouse. Guests are panicking. What do you do?
You apologize through interpreters. The elders appreciate it.
You find a weapons cache under the floor.
He orders an immediate exit. Smart.
You suspect someone in the partner force is leaking your mission plans to the enemy. How do you test it?
The enemy reacts to the fake plan. Leak found.
Your commanding officer {co} wrote a mediocre fitness report that could hurt your promotion. You believe it's unfair. What do you do?
He revises it after you show your results.
The reviewing officer sides with you.
You're planning a multi-team operation in {country}. Your staff wants a complex plan. Your instincts say simple. What do you choose?
The enemy adapts faster than your simple plan.
The partner unit you trained graduates their first commando class. Their general wants you to speak. What's your message?
The soldiers chant your name. Their general beams.
You're offered a staff job at headquarters. It's great for promotion but you'd leave your team. What do you do?
The team appreciates it. HQ remembers.
During a night exfil, {buddy} is missing. The helicopter is waiting, and enemies are closing in. What do you do?
You find him with a broken leg. Everyone gets out.
You find him, but you're both hit on the way back.
Nobody gets left behind. Except today.
A captured fighter claims he knows about an imminent attack. A partner officer suggests 'harsh methods'. What do you do?
Your interrogator gets the info through rapport.
You get intel. You lose your soul a little.
Your training budget is cut 40%. You must choose what to keep: dive training, sniper school, or language courses. What stays?
Your helicopter takes fire and does a hard landing. Everyone's alive but dazed. The enemy is coming. What do you do?
You reach a ridgeline and hold.
You've missed three anniversaries and your spouse is moving out. {co} offers you leave right before an operation. What do you do?
You save your marriage. The op goes fine without you.
The op is a success. Your house is empty.
You're sent to train with a foreign special forces unit. Their methods are rough and their humor rougher. How do you fit in?
You outlast them on a march. Friends for life.
They push you past your limits. You end up in medical.
Your battalion commander {co} wants to send your team into an operation you believe is poorly planned. What do you do?
He adjusts the plan. Thanks you later.
It works out. You were wrong.
It goes exactly as badly as you feared.
You must write award recommendations for your team. One Marine was brave but disliked by command. How do you write it?
He gets his medal. Command grumbles.
Your team finds a huge weapons cache. Some partner officers want to keep part of it. How do you handle it?
A huge explosion. The partner officers sulk.
The weapons show up in enemy hands.
Your briefing to the task force commander has a typo putting your team 10 km from the real target. You notice mid-brief. What do you do?
Air support plans around the wrong grid. Yikes.
The promotion board is reviewing your record. Your mentor offers to call a board member. What do you do?
Promoted. You'll never know if it was fair.
The board member reports it. Ugly.
An aid worker is held hostage in {country}. Your team is ready. Intel says guards rotate at 0300. When do you hit?
Hostage rescued alive. Zero friendly casualties.
The guards were alert. Heavy fighting.
The hostage is moved before you arrive.
You find a better entry point. Success.
A partner commander wants your team to support an assault on a village. Your legal advisor says the target list is shaky. What's your call?
The assault is canceled. Later, the list proves mostly wrong.
You only engage confirmed fighters. Clean operation.
The limits are ignored the moment shooting starts.
Your team has run raids five nights straight. Higher wants one more tonight. Your Marines are making mistakes. What do you do?
Approved. The next raid is flawless.
A tired mistake gets you hurt.
You lead a visit, board, search and seizure on a suspected weapons smuggling dhow at night. The crew is acting jumpy. How do you board?
Crew surrenders instantly. Rockets found in the hold.
A crewman fires from the wheelhouse.
They dump the cargo overboard while you talk.
As {rank}, you command a Raider battalion. Congress wants MARSOC cut to save money. You're asked to testify. What do you emphasize?
Budget saved. Senators praise the Raiders.
You're asked to shift Raiders from counterterrorism to great-power competition. Some old operators resist. How do you lead the change?
The force adapts. History will thank you.
You visit the family of a Raider killed under your command. His father is angry and blames you. What do you say?
He calms down. You stay in touch for years.
He doesn't want to hear it. Not yet.
A news story reveals misconduct by Raiders under your command. Your boss wants to know how you'll respond. What's your plan?
You clean house. Trust restored slowly.
More stories come out. You're relieved.
You represent US special operations at an allied summit. A foreign general proposes a joint mission with risky terms. What do you say?
The mission struggles on unclear command.
After 26 years, you're being considered for general. Your body is wrecked and your family wants you home. What do you do?
Not selected. Time to plan retirement.
You hang up the uniform with honors.
You're asked to dedicate a memorial for fallen Raiders, including some you sent into battle. What do you say?
It takes a long time. Nobody leaves.
Your battalion's injury rates are climbing and operators are burning out. Training tempo is to blame. What do you do?
Strength coaches and physical therapists work miracles.
You brief senior leaders on a sensitive operation in {country}. One asks a question you can't answer. What do you do?
Honesty is valued at this level.
Someone knows the real answer. Embarrassing.
A former Raider you served with as a captain calls you at midnight. He's out of the service and sounds like he's in crisis. What do you do?
You get him to a VA program. He's still alive years later.
He thanks you, flatly. You worry for weeks.
At a family reunion, your uncle insists Raiders are just 'Navy SEAL wannabes'. Everyone is watching. What do you do?
He doesn't listen, but your aunt is impressed.
He taps out at 12. You do 80.
He pulls a muscle. Now it's your fault.
You eat potato salad in peace.
{buddy} wants the team to pool money for a big lottery jackpot. Everyone's in. Are you?
You actually win a small share!
The team watches a military action movie. It's wildly inaccurate. {buddy} is yelling at the screen. Do you join in?
You keep a mental list of errors.
A Gold Star family organizes a memorial ruck. It's 22 miles on a weekend. Will you go?
Your feet are destroyed. Your heart is full.
The family sends a thank-you note.
A kid at a Veterans Day parade asks if you've ever been scared. What do you tell him?
His dad nods. The kid looks amazed.
He thinks you're a superhero. It's a lie.
A local gym influencer challenges you to a pull-up contest on camera. Do you accept?
You win. The video goes viral.
He wins. The video still goes viral.
RASP day one at Fort Moore. A cadre screams that half of you will quit by Friday. He's looking at you. What will you do?
You become furniture. Furniture doesn't get smoked. Mostly.
'HOOAH, SERGEANT!' He moves on, almost impressed.
He did not ask you a question. You learn that in the front-leaning rest.
A cadre demands you recite the Ranger Creed, all six stanzas, right now. You know five of them. What will you do?
The sixth stanza comes back mid-sentence. Rangers lead the way.
You blank on 'Readily will I display...' and spend an hour remembering it in the dirt.
Honesty earns pushups and an assignment to recite it 50 times tonight.
RASP 12-mile ruck, 3 hours to make it. Mile 9 and your legs are concrete. What will you do?
You cross with four minutes to spare and immediately lie in the gravel.
Your hamstring locks. You miss the time hack.
Steady was too slow by 90 seconds.
RASP combat water survival. Blindfolded, full kit, walk off the high dive. What will you do?
Splash, drop the rifle-free gear, swim out. Easy. Ish.
You panic underwater. Divers pull you out.
The cadre helps you off. With his boot.
Week three of RASP. Your shins are cracked with stress fractures. Medical offers you a recycle. What will you do?
Six weeks of healing, then you do it all again. Smarter this time.
You graduate on broken legs. Legendary, and stupid.
A shin snaps on a run. Medical drop.
RASP graduation. A Ranger places the tan beret on your head. {buddy} didn't make it. What will you do?
{buddy} says they'll be back next class. You believe it.
Big steak, bigger bar tab. Worth it.
{buddy} from a regular infantry unit says Rangers are 'just infantry with good PR.' What will you do?
You buy him a beer. Quiet confidence.
You smoke him on a 10-miler. He buys the beer.
Monday formation. Your haircut is three days old and the first sergeant says it's 'luxurious.' What will you do?
High and tight, back to standard.
You lose. You always lose this one.
Turn-in after the range. The armorer rejects your rifle for the fourth time. 'Carbon in the bolt carrier.' What will you do?
Your squad leader hands you the M240 machine gun for a 15-mile movement. Nobody else wants it. What will you do?
Your shoulders hate you. Your squad leader remembers.
Somebody left a door unlocked. The whole platoon is getting smoked. {buddy} whispers it was you. What will you do?
You own it. The smoke session ends sooner. Respect gained.
Ranger School, Darby phase. You're graded patrol leader and your squad is stumbling in the dark. What will you do?
You hit the objective on time. GO.
Ranger School, mountains of north Georgia. Freezing rain, 90 lb ruck, three hours of sleep in four days. What will you do?
You make it to Florida phase.
Your peers rank you high. That matters.
Florida phase. Waist-deep swamp at night. Something big just splashed nearby. What will you do?
It was probably a log. Probably.
It was not a log. Gator bite.
The squad bumps into you. Swearing ensues.
Day 50 of Ranger School. You see a vending machine in the woods and try to buy a soda from a tree. What will you do?
{buddy} slaps you. 'It's a tree, man.' You laugh like a maniac.
The RI writes it up for a hilarious after-action.
Ranger School peer evals. Your squad wants to 'peer' the guy who keeps falling asleep on watch. What will you do?
He gets recycled. Harsh, but he was endangering the patrol.
He stays. He thanks you. He falls asleep again.
Ranger School graduation. Your mom pins the tab on your shoulder. You've lost 30 pounds. What will you do?
Two pizzas, a cake, and a gallon of milk. Your stomach rebels.
Ranger School. You find a granola bar in an old fighting position. Eating it is a 'major minus.' What will you do?
Best granola bar of your life.
An RI sees the wrapper. Major minus.
You dream about it for weeks.
First deployment to {country}. Your first night raid. Your heart is pounding as the helicopter descends. What will you do?
You stack, flow, clear your corner. Exactly like training.
Shot through the arm on the breach.
A team leader shoves you forward. You recover. You'll be better.
Clearing a compound in {country}, you push into a room alone. A man is reaching under a mattress. What will you do?
He freezes. It was a cell phone. You did it right.
killed clearing a room in a night raid
He had a grenade. You saved the stack.
Combat jump onto an airfield in {country}. 500 feet, night, and your static line is tangled with another jumper. What will you do?
Free. Canopy opens. You hit the runway and roll.
You land hard on asphalt. Broken leg.
Reserve opens. You land off-target but alive.
killed in a combat parachute accident
Airfield seizure. Your job: clear the runway of vehicles and obstacles before the first C-17 lands in 30 minutes. What will you do?
You drive the truck off the runway. Planes land on time.
Field training at Hunter Army Airfield. The sand fleas are eating you alive. What will you do?
Your team leader nods. You're itchy for a week.
You hide the bug spray. {buddy} notices.
Joint Base Lewis-McChord. It's been raining for 40 straight days. Your gear smells like a swamp. What will you do?
Your barracks room becomes a laundromat.
Friday night in Savannah. {buddy} wants to drive back to Hunter after six beers. What will you do?
Uber home. {buddy} is mad, then thankful.
You make it back. You promise never again.
He crashes into a parked car. MPs.
You failed a PT test by 3 points and the battalion is threatening to RFS you. What will you do?
You crush the retest. Stay in batt.
You fail again. Back to regular Army.
He gets you a second chance.
You're carrying the breaching charge. The door is metal and thicker than expected. What will you do?
Door gone. So is the doorframe. Good enough.
Overpressure rattles your brain. Mild TBI.
Door holds. The team goes to a window.
Combatives tournament. You're matched against a former college wrestler. What will you do?
Rear-naked choke. He taps. The company goes wild.
He suplexes you. Your company winces.
You don't win, but you don't get tapped.
{buddy} snuck a handle of whiskey into the barracks. Alcohol is banned. Inspection is tomorrow. What will you do?
{buddy} mourns the whiskey. You both pass inspection.
JMPI before a training jump. You realize your reserve handle is rubber-banded wrong. What will you do?
Fixed. He thanks you for paying attention.
Main opens fine. Reserve not needed.
{buddy} is about to fail a land nav test and asks to follow you. It's an individual event. What will you do?
{buddy} fails. You feel bad, but it's on them.
An RI saw. Integrity violation for both.
Patrol base, 0400. You've slept 2 hours in 3 days. Your eyes close mid-sector scan. What will you do?
You wake up with nobody noticing.
Team leader finds you asleep. Article 15.
A grey-haired veteran of the 1993 Mogadishu battle speaks at your company. He asks if anyone has questions. What will you do?
He says fear never left, he just stopped listening to it. You write that down.
You listen. The room is dead silent.
{country}. Your squad is pinned by fire from a rooftop. Your team leader yells 'Suppress!' What will you do?
Your rounds keep their heads down. Squad maneuvers.
Your 40mm lands right on the rooftop. Silence.
As team leader, a private keeps failing standards. He's a good kid. The platoon sergeant asks your opinion on RFS. What will you do?
He goes to the 82nd. He'll do fine there.
He fails again. Your judgment is questioned.
You make squad leader. The previous one was beloved. Your guys keep comparing you. What will you do?
Six months later, they compare the next guy to you.
Night raid in {country}. Your team stacks on a door. You hear a woman and children inside. What will you do?
Interpreter calls them out. Women and kids exit. Clean.
A fighter used them as cover.
A child is injured in the breach.
A fighter barricaded in a room has already wounded one Ranger. What will you do?
He refuses. Now you need another plan.
Clean assault. Bronze Star with V.
Your squad finds the high-value target hiding in a spider hole. He's begging. What will you do?
The working dog attached to your squad alerts on a wall. The handler says 'something's there.' What will you do?
A fighter pops out of a hide behind you.
The Chinook carrying your squad lands hard. Smoke fills the cabin. Two Rangers aren't moving. What will you do?
Everyone out before the fire. Commendation.
Others handle the casualties. Perimeter holds.
You're a sniper team leader. A man on a rooftop is talking on a radio and watching your assault force. What will you do?
He moves off. Assault force adjusts.
He called in an RPG team.
Your Ranger medic is down and {buddy} is bleeding badly. Everyone in the regiment is trained in first responder care. What will you do?
Tourniquet, chest seal, needle decompression. {buddy} lives.
You do everything right. {buddy} doesn't make it.
The medic is only stunned. He takes over.
Twelve deployments in nine years. Your hands shake when you're not working. What will you do?
You start sleeping. Your squad notices you're calmer.
Thirteenth deployment. The shakes get worse.
You move to a training unit. The quiet is strange.
After years as a breacher, you're forgetting words and getting headaches daily. What will you do?
TBI diagnosis. Treatment helps. You're off the breach team.
Your battalion picks you and {buddy} for the Best Ranger Competition. 60 hours, nonstop events. What will you do?
You finish, but in the middle of the pack.
'I will never leave a fallen comrade.' A Ranger's body is in a building still taking fire. What will you do?
You bring him home. Silver Star.
The body is lost for 2 days.
Your squad raids a compound. Bad grid. It's a family of farmers. Everyone's terrified. What will you do?
You arrange condolence money. The family accepts.
A wounded enemy fighter lies in the courtyard. Your medic is busy. What will you do?
He lives and becomes a valuable source.
He dies. Was it your call?
Exfil helicopter is taking fire. The pilots say 60 seconds or they leave. Two guys are still clearing. What will you do?
You drag them back in 55 seconds.
One misses the bird. Second exfil required.
You catch a Ranger in your squad selling extra ammo to a civilian contact on base. What will you do?
It comes out later. You're both punished.
You keep saying 'what?' Your wife says the TV is too loud. What will you do?
You're the new platoon sergeant. Your lieutenant is fresh out of Ranger School and very confident. What will you do?
He becomes a great officer, crediting you years later.
He learns hard lessons. The platoon suffers.
Divorce papers arrive by email while you're in {country}. Your team needs you tonight. What will you do?
You do the mission. You fall apart after.
He listens. It helps a little.
Mid-firefight, a fighter steps out with hands up. {buddy} raises his weapon. What will you do?
He's taken prisoner. Laws of war upheld.
You find a laptop and cash on the objective. A teammate suggests pocketing the cash. What will you do?
Your 60mm mortar section must fire within 30 meters of friendlies. The math is tight. What will you do?
A private in your squad gets a DUI downtown. The first sergeant asks if you knew he had a problem. What will you do?
Honest answer. Lessons learned for everyone.
Your platoon is pinned. AC-130 says rounds would land 40 meters from you. What will you do?
Perfect fires. Platoon saved. Silver Star.
A grenade lands in the room with your fire team. Nowhere to throw it back. What will you do?
The grenade's fuse was partly defective. You live, badly hurt. Medal of Honor.
killed shielding teammates from a grenade
Your team survives because of you.
Your team holds a building corner while the platoon evacuates wounded. Fighters are massing. What will you do?
You hold until the last bird leaves. Distinguished Service Cross.
killed holding a corner during evacuation
Your squad leader says you need your tab to keep advancing. You've been putting it off. What will you do?
{buddy} died on the last deployment. His family asks you to speak at the funeral. What will you do?
You tell the story of {buddy} carrying you through RASP. Everyone cries.
You can't. You stand in the back.
Combat jump. Your squad lands scattered across the drop zone. Enemy fire coming from the tower. What will you do?
You gather six Rangers and take the tower.
As first sergeant, you must decide whether to pass a soldier with a positive drug test for Ranger school. What will you do?
He fails again. Your judgment questioned.
Your first day as a Ranger platoon leader. Your platoon sergeant has 9 combat deployments; you have zero. What will you do?
He respects you for it. Partnership forms.
You smoke everyone on the run. Grudging respect.
They roll their eyes behind your back.
You get a raid tasking with 3 hours until launch. Intel is thin. What will you do?
You're planning an airfield seizure in {country}. Do you jump in or air-land? What will you do?
Fast and surprising. Airfield seized in 20 minutes.
First plane takes fire on the runway.
You brief a two-star general on tonight's raid plan. He wants 'more aggression.' What will you do?
Weather is marginal for the helicopter infil. The target is only there tonight. What will you do?
The AC-130 overhead reports 'squirters' fleeing your target. Some might be civilians. What will you do?
You follow them to a second compound. Bonus target.
Ranger Orientation Program for officers. Your peers include a West Point first captain and a former college athlete. What will you do?
You all pass. Friends for life.
You have to call the parents of a private killed on your raid. What will you do?
Hardest call of your life. The father thanks you.
They wanted to hear your voice.
A private in your platoon did something heroic. Higher wants to downgrade the award. What will you do?
He gets the Silver Star he earned.
Intel says the target compound is empty of civilians. Your gut says otherwise. What will you do?
Drone spots a wedding. Raid postponed. Good call.
You take command of a Ranger rifle company. The previous commander was fired. What will you do?
You learn what went wrong. You fix it.
Your company's new radios fail during a raid. Squads can't talk. What will you do?
A female officer who earned her tab joins your company. Some NCOs are grumbling. What will you do?
Standard is standard. She earned the tab. Grumbling stops.
You're the battalion S3 (operations officer). Three missions, two helicopters. What will you do?
An American contractor is held in {country}. Your company is tasked. What will you do?
Your battalion commander rates you second of six captains. You want top block. What will you do?
Training jump at night. Winds above limits. Your men want to jump. What will you do?
A Ranger in your company is accused of misconduct on deployment. He's a star performer. What will you do?
Your company has done 40 raids in 60 days. The men are exhausted. Higher wants more. What will you do?
A documentary crew wants to film your company. PAO approves. What will you do?
Your detainees will be transferred to a partner prison known for torture. What will you do?
You're chosen to teach young lieutenants. A student is clearly struggling. What will you do?
Your company's vehicle convoy is ambushed. Lead vehicle is burning. What will you do?
You flank and destroy them. Bronze Star with V.
Major's board. Your file is good but not great. A mentor offers to call the board president. What will you do?
Your spouse says you've missed every birthday for four years. What will you do?
You take command of the 75th Ranger Regiment. Op tempo is crushing. What will you do?
You push back on some missions. Readiness rises.
A Ranger was killed by friendly fire. Higher wants to report it as enemy action. What will you do?
Family learns truth. You keep integrity.
Pentagon wants to cut the regiment's budget. What will you do?
Media wants your thoughts on Mogadishu at the anniversary. What will you do?
Three Rangers took their own lives this year. What will you do?
The Pentagon wants more Rangers. They suggest lowering RASP standards. What will you do?
Congress asks if Rangers are being over-deployed. What will you do?
The Ranger Memorial adds new names this year. You give the address. What will you do?
Twenty minutes. The silence is profound.
Your command sergeant major disagrees with your new policy publicly. What will you do?
A report surfaces of hazing in one battalion. What will you do?
After 26 years, you're offered a final command or retirement. What will you do?
Tan beret folded away. A peaceful life.
Ranger Rendezvous at Fort Moore. Old Rangers, young Rangers, beer. What will you do?
You meet a Vietnam Ranger. He buys your beer.
St. Patrick's Day in Savannah. The whole city is green and so is {buddy}. What will you do?
{buddy} makes it home. You're a hero.
A hurricane is bearing down on Hunter Army Airfield. What will you do?
Karaoke night. {buddy} dares you to perform the Ranger Creed to a power ballad. What will you do?
A third-grade class sends cards and candy. One card says 'Please don't die.' What will you do?
You tweak your back during a max deadlift. What will you do?
A kid at the airport sees your tan beret and asks if you're a superhero. What will you do?
'No, just a soldier who trains hard.' He salutes you.
You give him a scroll patch. He'll remember forever.
You're an airman at an air station waiting for an A-School slot. The swimmers there run a brutal prep workout and invite you. Do you go?
